notes: Two readings I cannot separate. (a) THRU by the flat-profile rule: the chain stays on its ~2e4 plateau to its last point and nothing electron-like leaves the end; 39014 is then a duplicate piece hugging the body. (b) STM_ONLY with an undershoot on a hooked end: the fit stops at the apex of a ~6 cm hook and 39014 is the returning leg carrying the Bragg peak (~3x plateau) at its far end, 5.7 cm back, so the real stop is at 39014 far end. (b) is favoured by the charge ending in every plane mid-volume and the Bragg-shaped climb; against it, the outgoing leg shows no approach to a peak, the return retraces the body within ~1-2 cm, and a stop here implies an upward-going particle. 39014 tagged muon under both readings (body duplicate or muon end).
evidence: 181 cm chain with both ends inside: the lower "entry" end is at (-34.8, 69.7, 257.6) in APA2, 62 cm above the bottom face, and the fit stop is the upper end at (-64.5, 198.7, 180.6) in APA0, 180 cm from the nearest face, 62 cm from the cathode and 50 cm from the APA seam. f_meas shows measured charge ending at the stop in U, V and W with no dead band and nothing continuing past it, so the charge really ends here. evidence: 49.5 cm single-segment track entering through the back face (7.4 cm from z=462, y=142) and stopping 26 cm from the nearest face (z), 70 cm from the cathode and 205 cm from the APA seam, at x=72, y=102, z=436, i.e. in APA3 (no known deficit). The dQ/dx profile is ragged on a ~60-70k plateau (one 1.1e5 cluster at s~7 cm) and over the last ~3 cm climbs steeply from ~55k to ~1.65e5 at the last point, following the muon reference curve; no collapse after it, so the pin stays at the fit end. No arm leaves the stop: the chains two Michel objects, 295004 and 296005, are each a 2-point, zero-extent clump whose nearest point is 3.2-3.3 cm from the stop (one sideways at cos_fwd -0.14 with 93k, one partly forward at +0.53 with 33k; the three stop azimuths put them ~2-3 cm off either side of the star). Being zero-size separate clumps with a ~3 cm gap to the last fit point, I read them as detached dots rather than an attached electron trunk, so gamma, not michel. Four more isolated compact specks all clear of the short body line: 292001 (5 pts, 26.7 cm, ~26 cm off-axis), 293002 (52 cm, forward), 294003 (56 cm, forward), 297006 (58 cm, forward, just inside the ~60 cm radius); under the STM_ONLY capture-gamma rule these are gamma in any direction, and the pattern (no trunk, several scattered specks) reads like a capture cascade. f_meas shows the track ending cleanly in all planes with no dead band near the stop.

About 140 cm; enters through the top 1.1 cm from y = 606 at z = 232.6 (right at the APA seam, entry side only) and stops at (-328.4, 517.5, 159.3): 29.5 cm from the anode face (nearest face), 88.5 cm below the top, 326 cm from the cathode, 72 cm from the seam, in APA0. The track is almost isochronous (x runs -332 to -328 over 140 cm; f_meas shows everything inside time slices ~1330-1345), which explains the low absolute charge (APA0 plus near-isochronous imaging, a wide ghost-like image spread in the 3-D frames) and a ragged profile. dQ/dx: about 1-2e4 from 12 to 30 cm (a gap-like dip at 10-11 cm, a bump to 3.5e4 at 36 cm), then 2.7-3.5e4 over the last 9 cm climbing slightly to the fit end; at most a weak, ragged rise, not decisive on its own. The verdict rests on topology: 57010 (6.45 cm, cos_fwd +0.98, mean dqdx 12951 vs the muon chain 28377) leaves the fit end straight ahead with a slight downward kink in the e azimuth; its charge peaks at the junction (|s| about 1, ~4e4) and falls steadily to near zero by |s| about 7 going outward. That is the ordinary forward-Michel shape (below the muon plateau, falling as it goes out), not a hot tip (not several times plateau, not a couple of cm, charge does not rise at its far end). No charge continues past the arm in any plane of f_meas (W ends at channel ~7205, nothing to 7100). No overshoot: no peak-then-collapse inside the fit, so the pin stays. 57001/57007 are pdg-13 pieces extending the muon body to the entry at the far end (209+12 = 221 chain points); 57006 is a delta ray on the body near the entry. Hard because the muon profile alone is weak on this isochronous APA0 track; the arm could in principle be the muon tail, but its falling charge argues electron.

Short object: 39.6 cm of chain but only ~23 cm entry-to-stop displacement. Enters 5.1 cm below the top (y = 600.9) and ends at (-108.1, 582.3, 195.3): 23.7 cm below the top (nearest face), 105.6 cm from the cathode, 35.7 cm from the APA seam, 250 cm from the anode, in APA0. The fitted path zigzags in the b/c azimuths (a hook about 4-8 cm before the end where the path doubles back and then turns forward again), though the e azimuth shows one coherent spine with wiggles, so I read it as one track, not MESSY. Profile (APA0, low scale): ~1-2e4 over 30-40 cm, a bump to 5e4 at s ~ 28 (at the 38012 delta-ray junction), ~1e4 from 15-22 cm, near-zero partial points at 5-8 cm, then a five-point climb over the last ~3 cm from 1.3e4 to 7.6e4 at the fit end, several times the track own plateau and shaped like the muon curve: a Bragg rise. Nothing electron-like leaves the end: every near piece (38005/38007/38011/38010, 38012) has cos_fwd -0.91 to -1.0 on the body behind the stop; f_meas shows no charge past the end in any plane and no dead channels at the stop. No hot tip (no forward piece at all) and no peak-then-collapse, so the pin stays. Three survey-only specks, isolated and 27+ cm clear of the body line, 44-57 cm out (151013 at 46.8 cm cos 0.57, 152014 at 57 cm cos 0.16, 153015 a 2-point no-charge speck 43.6 cm out beyond the entry end near the top): capture gammas under the STM_ONLY isotropic rule, all uncertain. 38001 (chain calls it shower) is the entry stub on the body line at the far end, tagged muon. Hard because the path is wiggly, the absolute charge is very low, and the rise rests on the last ~3 cm; the competing reading is a low-energy scattering object or MESSY imaging.

About 198 cm of chain; enters at (-352.0, 262.2, 9.1), 6 cm inside the anode face and 8.9 cm from the front face (side entry at that corner), runs nearly parallel to the anode and stops at (-338.9, 116.3, 86.6): 19.1 cm from the anode face (nearest), 109 cm above the bottom, 336 cm from the cathode, 144 cm from the APA seam, in APA0. dQ/dx: ragged plateau ~4-6e4 with dips to ~1-2e4 at 10-16 cm and 30-35 cm, then a clean climb over the last ~6 cm (4.9e4 -> 6.8e4 -> 1.09e5 -> 1.2e5 -> peak 1.45e5 at s ~ 2.5) that follows the muon reference curve; after the peak 1.1e5, 9.7e4, 7.3e4 (still above plateau) and one last partial point at ~0.6e4. That is ordinary end smearing plus a single partial point, not a sustained collapse, so no overshoot and the pin stays. The last segment 27008 curls in a small hook (18.6 cm long inside 10.7 cm of the stop) with the hot points at the star end, so the hook is the muon own end-of-range scatter. Nothing is attached at or past the stop: no forward piece (no hot tip to check), and f_meas shows the track ending at W ~7060 with no continuation and no dead channels at the end. Three 2-point specks, all detached: 129009 at 16 cm (cos_fwd -0.64, ~12 cm off the body line and ~11 cm nearer the anode in x), 130010 at 30 cm (~20 cm off the line), 131011 at 60 cm forward-side (~49 cm off the line). All clear of the body line and isolated: capture gammas under the STM_ONLY isotropic rule; 131011 at the 60 cm edge is the least certain. 27005/27006 are the muon body, 27007 a delta ray on the body near the entry.

About 429 cm; enters through the back face (z = 457.6, 4.7 cm inside) high in the detector and stops deep inside at (-257.5, 255.0, 303.4): 100.5 cm from the nearest face (anode), 247 cm above the bottom, 255 cm from the cathode, 72 cm from the APA seam, in APA2 but mid-height, far from its bad bottom/far-z corner; f_meas shows the track fully imaged to its end in all three planes with no dead channels there, so no coverage hole. dQ/dx sits on a ragged plateau ~5.5-6.5e4 (one bump to 1.03e5 at 23-24 cm), then climbs over the last ~8 cm (7.5e4 -> 8.5-9.2e4 -> 1.04e5 -> peak 1.23e5 at s ~ 2.5) right along the muon reference curve; after the peak 1.07e5, 8.1e4, then the last two points at 4e4 and 2.6e4 within the final ~0.7 cm. That end drop is under 1 cm, not a sustained collapse over several cm into a bridged piece, so no overshoot and the pin stays. The last few cm hook by roughly 90 deg in the c azimuth (straight in d and e): end-of-range scatter carrying the hot points. Nothing attached at or past the stop and no forward piece (no hot tip). Three 2-3 point specks, all isolated and 26-35 cm off the body line: 189012 at 28.8 cm (cos_fwd -0.37), 182010 at 42 cm forward (cos 0.78), 186011 at 51 cm (cos -0.71); capture gammas under the STM_ONLY isotropic rule. 37009 is the upper muon body; 37008 is a delta ray on the body 184 cm back.

About 144 cm; enters through the top 2.7 cm from y = 606 and stops at (336.2, 498.2, 356.8): 21.8 cm from the anode face (nearest), 108 cm below the top, 334 cm from the cathode, 126 cm from the APA seam, in APA3. dQ/dx: plateau ~5-6.5e4 (ragged, one pair at 9.5e4 near 20 cm), 5-8e4 over the last 10 cm, then a textbook Bragg rise over the last ~2 cm (1.06e5 -> 1.23e5 -> 1.52e5 -> 1.63e5 -> 1.75e5 at the last point), sitting on the muon reference curve and peaking at the fit end: no overshoot (no peak-then-collapse) and the pin stays. The other seven pdg-13 rows are the muon body up to the top entry.

About 237 cm; enters 10.1 cm below the top at (-124.5, 595.9, 298.1) and stops at (-161.3, 418.6, 422.1): 40.2 cm from the back face (nearest), 159 cm from the cathode, 191 cm from the APA seam, 197 cm from the anode, in APA2 at mid-height (y = 419), far from its bad bottom/far-z corner; f_meas shows the track fully imaged to its end with no dead channels there. dQ/dx: ragged plateau ~5.5-7e4 with bumps to ~1e5 at 7-9 cm and again at 17-18 cm, a dip to 2.5-3.5e4 over 3-5.5 cm (the last few cm bend ~30 deg in the e azimuth and read low there), then a climb 4.8e4 -> 8e4 -> 1.73e5 over the last ~1.2 cm, about 3x the plateau at the end: a ragged Bragg rise ending at the fit end. I did not move the pin: the 7-9 cm bump is no higher than the 17-18 cm plateau bump, and what follows the dip is the hottest charge on the track, not an electron-like piece. Nothing is attached at the stop (no hot-tip piece either). Past it are four detached specks, each with a clean charge-free gap to the stop in all three 3-D azimuths and in f_meas (W: track ends at ~9195/557, the nearest pair sits at 9218-9222/550): 216006 (10.6-11.7 cm, cos_fwd 0.6, ~9 cm off the body line, 1.3e4), 215005 (12.7 cm, cos 0.14, ~12 cm off the line, 6.5e3), 217007 (16 cm, cos -0.05, ~16 cm off the line), 213004 (58 cm, 2 points, no charge). By the attachment tie-break these are detached dots, so gamma not michel (capture gammas, isotropic, on this STM_ONLY). The chain calls 216006+215005 the Michel object; the competing reading is a Michel electron seen only as two faint detached pieces 11-13 cm out (STM_MICHEL), or a stop near 7 cm with the dip as a bridged gap. Medium because the end profile is ragged (dip then spike) and the two nearest dots sit just outside 10 cm.

295 cm chain, enters 1.2 cm inside the back face (z=461) and stops at (251,248,344) in APA3, 107 cm from the anode face (nearest face), 113 cm from the APA seam and 249 cm from the cathode: well contained. The dQ/dx profile sits on a ~55-75k plateau and climbs over the last ~5 cm to ~95k-1.2e5, following the muon reference curve; the last 3 points (~93-99k) are a little under the 4 cm peak, ordinary scatter, no sustained collapse, so the pin stays at the fit end. A connected three-segment arm (114003/114004/114008, 0 to 10.9 cm) leaves the stop at a sharp angle (roughly -z and +y, cos_fwd +0.1 to -0.34) and is clearly off the muon line in all three azimuths; its charge is 10k-55k, below the muon plateau and falling outward: an electron, the Michel. Three detached specks: 339010 (20 cm) and 347011 (17 cm) sit 11-17 cm off the body line and on the same side as the Michel arm (cos ~0.7 with the Michel direction) despite cos_fwd -0.67; 337009 (59-61 cm) lies almost exactly along the Michel direction: all gamma. 114007 is an 8 cm arm at the far (entry) end 224 cm away: delta / other. No dead region at the stop in W; the V dead band sits next to the stop but U and W show the Michel as real measured charge. The only soft calls are the two 16-20 cm specks, which are backward in cos_fwd but well clear of the body.

391 cm chain, enters through the top (y=606, d_face 0) near the x<0 anode and stops at (-122,325,259) in APA2 (not the bottom corner), 204 cm from the nearest face, 120 cm from the cathode and 28 cm from the APA seam: contained and away from both traps. The dQ/dx profile is a textbook Bragg rise: plateau ~55-65k, climbing smoothly along the muon reference curve from ~75k at 10 cm to ~1.2e5 at 1.5 cm and ~1.7e5 at the last point, no collapse after the peak, so the pin stays at the fit end. Nothing electron-like leaves the end: the fit end has a small few-cm hook in one azimuth (d) that is part of the muon cloud, no separate object is drawn there, and f_meas shows measured charge ending exactly where the predicted track ends in all three planes (no residual past the stop, no dead region at the end; the W dead channel crosses mid-track). The only nearby object is 255004, a 4-point 1.8 cm speck 47 cm out, cos_fwd -0.86 but ~22 cm off the body line in all three azimuths: isolated and compact, so a capture gamma (STM_ONLY rule, any direction); its tag is the softest part of the record. 56003 is a 3 cm delta on the body 272 cm up the track: delta / other.

173 cm chain, enters 0.7 cm inside the back face (z=462, y=584) and stops at (-199,437,440) in APA2 (upper part, not the bottom corner), 22.8 cm from the back face (nearest), 196 cm from the cathode and 209 cm from the APA seam. The dQ/dx profile climbs from a ~60-70k plateau to ~95-100k at 3-5 cm and ~1.4e5 at 1.5 cm, following the muon curve; the very last point (~1.03e5) is one point ~25% under the peak, ordinary scatter rather than a sustained collapse, so the pin stays at the fit end. A single attached 11.5 cm arm (50005, 0-9.5 cm) leaves the stop at a sharp angle (cos_fwd -0.25, going away perpendicular to the body in all three azimuths) at 40-60k, at or under the plateau: the Michel, clearly real measured charge in all three planes of f_meas (the hook at the end). Three detached 2-point specks at 29.5, 31 and 43 cm (222006, 224008, 223007) all lie on the Michel side, within ~20 deg of the Michel arm direction and roughly perpendicular to the muon (cos_fwd -0.01 to -0.34), well clear of the body line: gamma. 50001 is a 1 cm pdg-211 stub at the entry end 163 cm up: delta / other. No dead channel near the stop.

notes: NO_MEASUREMENT: APA2 bottom far-z corner coverage hole; dQ/dx is 0-15k along the whole 53 cm and U/W show no measured charge on the predicted track, no topology at the end.
evidence: 53 cm chain of only 26 fit points (37 image points) lying almost parallel to the drift direction at y=13, 5.7 cm above the bottom face along its whole length: entry (-62,13,451) and stop (-113,13,449), 13.7 cm from the back face, 110 cm from the cathode. The stop is in APA2 in its bottom far-z corner (y~13, z~449), exactly the coverage-hole region. The dQ/dx profile has essentially no measurement: four points at 5-15k at the fit end and a 15-24 cm stretch at 0-10k, all far below any muon plateau, with nothing in between; there is no plateau to rise from. f_meas confirms a coverage hole, not a collapse: in U and W the predicted track is a thin line with no measured charge along it, only V shows a small patch. In the three azimuths the sparse pieces (short segment, dots, entry and stop markers) are roughly collinear, so it reads as one sparsely imaged track rather than an EM blob, but there is no electron-like arm or object at the fit end and no Bragg information. The two 2-point specks sit on the body line (234004 at 25 cm, ~6 cm off the line; 235005 at 58 cm, ~6 cm past the far end, cos_fwd -0.97): delta / other. Competing readings: a fragment of a steeper track mostly lost in the hole (FRAG_THRU), or MESSY; neither can be supported from the charge.

40 cm chain entering 8.3 cm inside the x>0 anode face at mid height (349.6,197,442) and stopping at (329.5,175,427) in APA3, 28.5 cm from the anode face (nearest), 327 cm from the cathode and 196 cm from the APA seam. The dQ/dx plateau is ragged (~30-65k, with a 25-40k stretch at 15-35 cm and a 30-45k dip at 3-6 cm); the last two points climb to ~1.2e5 and ~1.35e5, about twice the plateau and on the muon curve: a short but real rise at the fit end, with no collapse after it, so the pin stays. The opposite (anode) end has no rise, so the direction is right. A 10 cm attached arm (127002, 0-9.3 cm, cos_fwd +0.46) leaves the stop at a sharp angle, mostly towards -x, clearly off the muon line in all three azimuths, at 0-65k (one 85k point at the junction, one hot point at its far end), at or under the plateau: the Michel, not a hot tip (10 cm long, not straight ahead, not several times the plateau), and real measured charge in U/V/W of f_meas. 324005 (21 cm, ~21 cm off the body, Michel side) and 323004 (39 cm, forward hemisphere, cos_fwd +0.33): gamma. 325006 (35 cm, cos_fwd -0.26, ~83 deg from the Michel direction, backward hemisphere though 33 cm off the body) reads as an unrelated direction: delta / other, the softest tag here. 126003 is a 2-point stub on the line just past the far (anode-side) end, continuing the muon: muon. No dead channels near the stop.

notes: Competing readings: (1) THRU, since a 2.4 cm collinear 5-point stub is thin evidence for an electron and the fit end has no rise; (2) the stop is at the 9-14 cm hump and the last ~9.5 cm of 50045 plus 50044 is a collinear Michel (would be an overshoot with pin ~9.5 cm, rejected because the fall is to plateau not below it and APA0 heights are untrustworthy); (3) FRAG_STM_MICHEL, since the chain begins mid-volume beside the 316 cm cluster C41 lying along its body.
evidence: 127 cm chain of 8 zig-zag segments running upward from (-235,31,98), 23 cm inside the bottom face (not a face entry), to a stop at (-219,103,155) in APA0, 95 cm from the nearest face, 217 cm from the cathode and 76 cm from the APA seam. The region is busy: the chain crosses a large unfitted cluster C41 (316 cm, on the body line 37-86 cm back) and a set of pdg-11 shower pieces 49-80 cm back, beside many partial points. The APA0 plateau is very low (~10-35k, segment means 5-24k) and wavy, with 1.5-2x humps at s~19, 35 and 41 cm. There is no rise at the fit end: the largest hump, ~65-73k, sits at s = 9-14 cm, and the profile then declines smoothly over ~8 cm to ~22k at s = 2 and stays there to the last point, i.e. it falls to the plateau, not well below it, and with no charge-free gap, so the overshoot signature is not met and the pin stays at the fit end. The verdict rests on topology: 50044, a 2.4 cm 5-point piece straight ahead (cos_fwd +0.92) at 22k falling to 12k outward, at or below the plateau, is the rubric ordinary forward-Michel case and not a hot tip; nothing else continues past the end in any azimuth. Everything else is backward or another object: 237042 (28 cm, cos_fwd -0.33), 159041 (55 cm, -0.9), 238043 (61 cm, -0.64), the pdg-11 shower pieces and C41: delta / other. No dead region at the stop end in any plane (the W dead channel is at the lower end). What made it hard: thin topology and an uninformative APA0 profile.

notes: Near-isochronous track (x constant to 0.5 cm over 192 cm); rule-2 rise read anyway, confidence capped at medium for that reason. Tag doubt: the 30-38 cm clump sits right past the far end of the upstream arm S33001 and may be that object s debris rather than capture gammas; if so the clump is delta / other and kind becomes none. Also odd: a 22 cm arm cannot be a knock-on delta from a muon 20 cm from its stop (T_max < 1 MeV), so S33001 is likely an isochronous-imaging artifact or a separate object.
evidence: 192 cm, enters through the top 1.9 cm from y=606 and stops mid-volume at y=432, 91.5 cm from the nearest face (z), 240 cm from the cathode, 140 cm from the APA seam, in APA2 (x<0, z>232, not the bottom corner). The dQ/dx plateau is ~50-60k; over the last ~10 cm it climbs to 1.1-1.4e5 (about 2.4x), following the muon curve, ragged but a clear rise. The last three points (s=0-1 cm) drop to 40-70k: a ~1 cm terminal dip with nothing past it for the fit to bridge, so ordinary scatter, pin left at the fit end. On STM_ONLY these isolated compact pieces within 60 cm are capture-gamma candidates in any direction: gamma.

notes: Michel piece is only 3.4 cm; STM_MICHEL vs STM_ONLY rests on it. Stop itself is well supported (rise + charge ends in all planes).
evidence: 280 cm, enters near the top (19.5 cm below y=606) and stops mid-volume at (145.5, 363.8, 95.1), 94.9 cm from the nearest face (z), 143 cm from the cathode, 136 cm from the APA seam, 212 cm from the anode, in APA1. S90004 (3.4 cm, 7 points) is attached at the fit end and leaves sideways/backward (cos_fwd -0.23); its charge starts at ~1.3e5 at the junction and falls through 50-70k to 13-25k going out, i.e. at or below plateau and falling, which is electron-like, not a hot muon tip, so michel. It is very short (~7 MeV-scale range), which is why this is medium rather than high: the competing reading is that it is only the splash of the muon Bragg peak and the item is STM_ONLY. notes: STM_MICHEL rests on a 2-point 0.1 cm speck 4 cm from the stop (within-5-cm rule); competing reading is STM_ONLY with all three specks capture gammas (kind detached dots). The stop itself is solid.
evidence: 507 cm, enters near the top (19 cm below y=606) and runs almost vertically down along the cathode side of the x>0 volume (x 11-22), stopping at (22.1, 130.4, 368.4): 93.9 cm from the nearest face (z), 122.8 cm above the bottom, 137 cm from the APA seam, 19.6 cm from the cathode, in APA3. Not a cathode crossing: the end is ~20 cm off x=0 and the last ~30 cm of track has a clear drift slope in f_meas (not isochronous there). dQ/dx plateau ~55-65k with two upstream dips at 29-32 and 41-43 cm; over the last ~10 cm it climbs through 80-100k to 1.23e5 at 1-4 cm and 1.68e5 at the last point, tracking the muon curve: a clear Bragg rise, no terminal collapse. notes: ANODE: face.x 6.4 cm (|x| 351.6), no rise; SEAM: also 3.5 cm from the APA seam; the chain entry at the bottom face is the natural exit of a downgoing muon entering here
evidence: 191 cm; the chain entry is at the bottom face (y face 0.3 cm) and the fit end is at (351.6, 147.1, 234.5): face.x 6.4 cm, i.e. |x| = 351.6 at the anode wire plane, and also only 3.5 cm from the APA seam, 139 cm above the bottom, in APA3 at the seam. Not isochronous (|dx|/L = 0.49). The geometry reads as a downgoing muon that enters through the x>0 anode here and leaves through the bottom. The profile has a ~4.5-5e4 plateau with isolated spikes at 11-13 cm (1.1-1.24e5) and 21-23 cm (1.45e5) where attached pieces meet the body, and the last 3 cm sit at 2.4-3.7e4, below the plateau: no rise at the end. No decay topology at the end: all three azimuths show the track running cleanly into the star; the long purple arm 110014 (+ 110007 / 110010) leaves the body 35-42 cm back and runs roughly parallel to it, ending ~17 cm short of the end (4 cm off axis), which is a delta / other, not stop-vertex activity; the survey specks 317016 / 318017 / 321018 are 44-51 cm back and 15-16 cm off the line. f_meas: the end is the lowest-time end (~slice 995, shortest drift) and all planes stop there, with a W dead band (~9278) at the end channel. An end at the anode and the seam with no rise: THRU. Non-chain rows are delta / other.

notes: FLAT_STOP: mid-volume end, own charge ends in U and W, nothing continues in 3-D; no rise, last 2 cm dip. Hidden other-flash blob caps confidence
evidence: 105 cm track coming down from near the back face (chain entry 11.7 cm from z=462, y=259) to the fit end at (86.3, 199.5, 404.1) in APA3 (x>0, z>232), mid-volume: 58 cm from the back face, 84 cm from the cathode, 173 cm from the seam, 272 cm from the anode face, 192 cm above the bottom. Not isochronous (x moves 63 cm). The dQ/dx over the last ~18 cm sits at ~4.5-8e4 with no climb, and the last 2 cm dip to ~2.5-3.3e4; further back the body carries scattered clumps at 1.1-1.5e5 (s=19-22, 32-33, 41-45) that look like delta activity, not a Bragg shape. So no rise; the terminal dip is short and there is nothing past the end for a fit to bridge to, so no overshoot. Rule 3: in f_meas the own charge ends at the fit end in U and W with no dead band there (the V track runs time-prolonged alongside the dead band at ch ~5597 over its whole length, not only at the end); the end is not at a face, the cathode or the seam; the three 3-D azimuths show a clean straight end with nothing continuing and no object starting at the stop. evidence: 124 cm track. Nothing lies above the fit end in any projection, so a downward cosmic could not have entered there: either the particle came up from the bottom and stopped at the fit end (the chain reading) or it was produced at the fit end and went down. The profile is APA0-broken: humps of 2.5-6e4 separated by near-zero troughs every ~10-15 cm all along (s 0-5, 22-25, 35-37), and the last ~5 cm reads ~0 - a trough, not a measurement, so no rise and no collapse can be read (no pin move). Topology at the fit end: 23002 (5.3 cm, 10 pts, 3.4e4, below the 4.3e4 body plateau) leaves the stop vertex and runs back along the body at ~30 deg (cos_fwd -0.86); in the e azimuth it is a separate line from the muon - an arm at the stop vertex running back, which v2 counts as the Michel. 145019 (2 pts, 6.4-6.7 cm, ~5.5 cm off the body line) sits across a visible charge-free gap: gamma. 146020 (4.4 cm, 8 pts, 11.8-12.8 cm, cos 0.94, 2.9e4) is detached and compact beyond 10 cm: gamma (no track continues beyond it, so it is not an upstream continuation). f_meas: the W end sits on a single dead channel (7097) with 146020 ~15 channels further; no band swallows the end. Chain delta and pdg-11 rows sit 16-42 cm back on the body: delta / other. MCS 234 vs range 302 MeV says low momentum.

notes: Tag doubt: 349012 (3 cm gap past the arm end) could be read as a gamma rather than the electron continuation; kind stays both either way because of 348011/347010.
evidence: 330 cm muon, enters through the back face (z = 456.9, d_face 5.4) at y = 441 and stops mid-volume at (93.2, 177.7, 313.9) in APA3: 148 cm from the nearest face, 90.7 cm from the cathode, 82.9 cm past the seam. The profile sits on a ~6-8e4 plateau and climbs to 1.0-1.1e5 at s 6-8 cm and 1.3-1.42e5 over the last ~2 cm, following the muon curve (a few 6-7e4 points at s 3-5 cm are scatter); the last point is the highest, no overshoot. 111002 (8.9 cm, 16 pts) leaves the stop vertex at a sharp kink (cos_fwd 0.44, ~90 deg in the c and d azimuths) and continues as 111003 (3.8 cm) to 11.7 cm; its charge starts at the shared Bragg point and settles at ~5.5-6.5e4, i.e. plateau, falling to ~4e4 - a muon at its Bragg peak cannot continue at MIP, so a second particle; not a hot tip (8.9 cm long, off-axis, not several times plateau), undershoot check negative. 349012 (1.2 cm, 4.2e4) sits just past the arm end on its line at 14.7 cm: electron continuation, michel. 348011 (2 cm, faint 5.9e3, 17 cm, cos 0.2) is a detached speck on the Michel side: gamma. 347010 (2 pts, 44 cm) lies ~36 deg from the Michel direction, on its side: gamma. 111004 and 111009 sit 137-263 cm back on the body: delta / other. f_meas: charge ends at the stop plus the arm in U, V and W; the V dead band at 6245 is on the body, not at the stop.

notes: NO_MEASUREMENT: fit end in U and W dead channels, profile interpolated. Leading alternative THRU: a downward cosmic whose upper part is lost where U and W are both dead, with the chain entry end (bottom, fork 56011) as the real stop candidate (REVERSED-type); second alternative STM_MICHEL by the v2 backward-arm rule if 56010 is real charge rather than a ghost.
evidence: 85 cm track imaged from only 129 points. The chain entry end is 5.4 cm above the bottom face (y = 13.0) and carries a fork (56011, 12.8 cm, 5.9e4, leaves the body end at a sharp angle); the fit end is the upper end at (-57.4, 71.7, 317.3) in APA2, low in the APA (y 72): 64 cm above the bottom, 54.9 cm from the cathode, 86.3 cm from the seam, 145 cm from the back face. With W and U both dead at the end, imaging cannot see a continuation, and the dQ/dx panel is a smooth interpolation (a hump to 6.5e4 at s 5 cm, zero from s 16-25 cm, a second hump at 40 cm), not a measurement: no rise, no collapse, no pin move. 56010 (11.8 cm, cos_fwd -0.93) runs back from the fit end doubling the body ~4 cm off it; in a dead-channel region with the track along the wires that is what an imaging ghost looks like, so I do not count it as decay topology. 283012 (2 pts, 5.7 cm) and 284013 (faint, 21 cm, back along the body) are specks. No verdict survives: the end is swallowed by dead channels (rule 3 fails) and topology is untrustworthy.

222 cm muon, its fitted entry 15 cm below the top (y = 590.9) near x = 32, stops mid-volume at (102.3, 405.1, 147.4) in APA1: 147 cm from the nearest face, 99.8 cm from the cathode, 83.6 cm from the seam. The only nearby object, 347026 (3 pts, 1.5 cm, 5.3e4), sits 11.5 cm from the stop at cos_fwd -0.3, i.e. ~11 cm off the body line, with a clean charge-free gap in all three azimuths and in f_meas (a separate blob ~20 U channels and ~20 W channels from the end): isolated compact piece, capture gamma. The chain delta and pdg-11 rows sit 49-129 cm back on the body: delta / other. f_meas: measured charge ends at the fit end in U, V and W; the nearest dead channels are single lines, none at the stop.

notes: Near-isochronous final 70 cm: rule 3 does not apply and the end is imaging-limited; the Michel is a 3-4 cm hook at plateau charge on a flat APA0 profile. Competing readings: STM_ONLY if the hook is the muon final scatter or a ghost of the isochronous sheet; UNCLEAR if the isochronous end is not trusted at all. Tag doubt: 136024 read as part of C325 rather than a gamma.
evidence: 195 cm muon, enters through the front face (z = 9.0, d_face 8.8) at y = 407 and stops mid-volume at (-155.1, 389.6, 175.9) in APA0: 175.7 cm from the nearest face, 152.6 cm from the cathode, 55.1 cm from the seam. The profile is APA0-low and ragged (2-6.5e4, plateau ~4.5e4) and stays flat over the last 10-20 cm: no rise, no collapse, no pin move. At the stop vertex 32022 (3.9 cm, 7 pts, 4.6e4 = plateau) leaves at a kink (cos_fwd -0.25, a sideways hook in the c and d azimuths): a muon at its end cannot continue at plateau, so I read it as a short electron; not a hot tip (sideways, plateau charge), undershoot check negative. 170025 (1.9 cm, compact, 21.6 cm, cos 0.76, past the stop) is detached: gamma. 136024 (58 cm) sits on the big neighbouring track C325 in the c and e azimuths: delta / other, as is C325 itself (222 cm separate cosmic, no dqdx, 43-60 cm away) and the 50 cm pdg-4 arm 32018 and pdg-11 rows 32017/32019 leaving the body 46-133 cm back. f_meas: measured charge ends at the fit end in U, V and W, no dead band; nothing continues within the window.

notes: Competing readings: STM_MICHEL with 300083 as a detached Michel and all arms read as delta rays (the hump at s 5-7 cm then a drop could be a Bragg peak with a short overshoot); or the fit end is a production vertex (steeply upward track, nothing above the end). The chain entry end is at the front face, so not a REVERSED stop candidate.
evidence: 318 cm track. The chain entry is at the front face (z = 2.7, d_face 2.5) low in the detector (y = 84) and the fit runs steeply UP (y-component ~0.85) to the fit end at (316.7, 312.9, 92.5) in APA1: 41.3 cm from the anode face, 92 cm from the front face, 138.5 cm from the seam, 314 cm from the cathode. Nothing lies above the fit end, so a downward particle would have to start there. The last ~60 cm is a web of pieces: in all three azimuths and in f_meas (a clump of ~20 vertices around the end in U, V, W) the body is crossed and paralleled by attached arms and pdg-11 shower pieces - 97025 (3.8-7 cm), 97056/97057 (4.4-8.4 cm, cos -0.71/-0.76, one at 5.8e4), 97055 (15 cm long, 7.5-19 cm), 97026 (9.8-15 cm), 97042, 97049 (25 cm shower piece at 37-55 cm) and a dozen specks 20-56 cm out. The profile reflects it: a 1.27e5 bump at s ~ 33 cm, a deep trough to ~0.7e4 at s 12-27 cm, a hump to 8.5e4 at s 5-7 cm and 2-3e4 over the last 3 cm - no single Bragg shape can be isolated. The chain Michel 300083 (4 cm) and 167072 sit 10-13 cm ahead, detached; with this much activity overlapping the last 20 cm I cannot say where the track ends or what leaves it. Busy stop: MESSY, every row delta / other.

notes: FLAT_STOP: APA0 profile unusable, stop decided by rule 3; competing reading STM_MICHEL with the collinear 5 cm low-charge stub 34008 as a forward Michel (the rubric calls such a stub weak topology), tagged muon here; an unrelated isochronous track crosses the event near the seam, far from the stop
evidence: 452 cm, shallow track that enters through the back face (z 461.6, d_face 0.7) near the top, crosses the APA seam ~130 cm before its end, and stops at (-237.1, 468, 100.9) in APA0: 100.6 cm from the front face, 121 cm from the anode, 138 cm below the top, 130 cm from the seam and 235 cm from the cathode, well inside. In APA0 the dQ/dx is ragged and patchy (0.05-0.75e5 with many low partial points): over the last 10 cm it sits at 0.2-0.4e5, below the 0.5-0.7e5 seen at s 9-14, with no rise, which I read as no usable measurement rather than a flat profile. Rule 3: f_meas shows the track charge ending at the same slice (t ~127) in U, V and W; a single dead W channel sits ~15 channels before the end, not over it; the end is far from every face, the seam and the cathode; and in the three stop azimuths nothing continues except 34008, a 5 cm stub carrying on nearly collinear (cos_fwd 0.98, at most a ~20 deg bend in one azimuth) at 23k, which I take as the muon running its last few cm, so the stop is at the stub end ~5 cm past the fit end. No arm leaves at an angle and no specks lie past the end. The side pieces 34009, 34014, 34017, 34018 are low-charge arms on the body 107-377 cm back: delta / other.

notes: NO_MEASUREMENT: near-isochronous 634 cm track (dx 18 cm), fit loops through a ghost sheet near the end, last 20 cm ~no charge. Leading alternative THRU (the owner called near-isochronous items THRU in calibration; 61047 below the end could be the continuation toward the bottom); STM_ONLY only if the end were trusted.
evidence: 634 cm chain, enters through the back face (z = 461.2, d_face 1.1) near the top (y = 588) and ends at (-251.1, 336.1, 55.6) in APA0: 55.4 cm from the front face, 107 cm from the anode, 175 cm from the seam, 249 cm from the cathode. The whole track is near-isochronous: x changes 18 cm over 634 cm, so in f_meas every plane shows it flat at t ~ 50-65, and the imaging produces a huge ghost sheet (20025 image points) around it in all three azimuths. Over its last ~80 cm the fitted path loops and doubles back through that sheet (body segments at cos_fwd -0.5 against the local tangent), so the fit end is not a trustworthy stopping point. The profile over the last 20 cm is essentially unmeasured: ~0 over the last 5 cm, rising only to 1-4e4 by s 20 cm, with no reference-curve shape anywhere. No decay topology: the only objects near the end are the pdg-4 row 61047 (45 cm, 10k, starting ~20 cm from the end and running away downward, directly below the stop) with 61048 at its far end, which could be another object or the muon itself continuing; I cannot tell which. Rule 3 does not apply to a near-isochronous track, there is no measurement to read a rise or a collapse from, and topology says nothing: UNCLEAR.

notes: Tag doubt: 188013 (2 pts, ~2 cm past the Michel arm end, 10.7 cm from the stop) read as the electron continuation; as a detached dot it would be gamma and the kind both.
evidence: 238 cm single-segment muon, enters through the top (y = 600.1, d_face 5.9) and stops at (320.6, 432.7, 207.0) in APA1: 37.4 cm from the anode face, 24 cm short of the APA seam, 173 cm below the top, 318 cm from the cathode - inside on every count. The profile sits on a ~5.5-7e4 plateau and climbs to 0.85-1.1e5 (about 1.5x) over the last ~5 cm, following the muon reference curve from below; ragged but a rise, last point 0.95e5, no collapse, so no pin move. 115007 (9.7 cm, 17 pts) leaves the stop vertex at a clear kink (cos_fwd 0.63; a V-shape in all three azimuths) at ~5e4, about plateau - a muon at its Bragg peak cannot continue at MIP, so a second particle, the right length for a Michel electron; not a hot tip (10 cm long, off-axis, plateau charge), undershoot check negative. 188013 (2 pts) sits ~2 cm past the arm end on the same line at 10.7-11.4 cm: the electron continuing, michel. No other objects. f_meas: measured charge ends with the arm in U, V and W; the nearest dead channels are far from the stop.

notes: ANODE: end at |x| = 352.0 (face.x 5.9), flat profile
evidence: 457 cm track from a chain entry 13 cm above the bottom face at (-104.7, 20.7, 424.7) to a fit end at (-352.0, 369.4, 359.6) in APA2: face.x 5.9 cm, |x| = 352.0, at the anode wire planes, 129 cm from the seam and 237 cm from the nearest y face. The profile is flat on a ~5e4 plateau through the last 40 cm: three low points (2.2-2.8e4) at 1-2 cm and a single last point at 1.05e5, which is one-point scatter, not a rise following the muon curve and not a peak-then-collapse. Charge runs to the low-time (anode) end in all three planes of f_meas, no dead band. Nothing continues or branches at the star in c/d/e. The only rows past the end are 34007 (0.2-0.9 cm straight on, no dqdx, 2 points), a degenerate row, and 183008, a 6-point speck 48 cm away at cos 0.29, unrelated. 35006 is a body delta ~283 cm back. An end at the anode with a flat profile and no decay topology: anode exit, the chain direction probably reversed for a downward cosmic that entered through the anode.

notes: ANODE: fit end at |x| 351.1 (face.x 6.9). Competing reading: an overshoot, with a muon stop near s 13 and 43008/43004 as a Michel beyond a low-charge bridge; rejected because the peak is weak and a stopper here would have travelled upward from the bottom face.
evidence: 142 cm track in APA2. The chain entry (-303.4, 8.0, 241.2) is 0.4 cm from the bottom face and the fit end (-351.1, 122.1, 253.8) has face.x 6.9, |x| 351, i.e. at the anode wire plane; 348.6 cm from the cathode and 23 cm from the APA seam in z. So both ends sit at faces, and a downward cosmic would enter at this anode end and leave through the bottom. The dQ/dx is a ~50-60k plateau with a small bump to ~72k at s 14-16, then falls to 10-37k at s 10-13, has no points at s 3-9, and reads 5-10k over the last 2.5 cm: the last ~10 cm chain piece 43010 averages 7k. There is no rise at the end, and the low stretch does not read as a stop signature. Near the end sit 43008, a 17.5 cm arm at 22k running back along the body 1-2 cm off it (d 2-11 cm, cos_fwd -0.92), and 43004, a 5 cm piece at 2-4 cm going sideways; U shows extra measured charge alongside the body and the U end sits at a dead band. These look like charge the fit path missed near the anode, not a clear electron. At the anode with no rise and no clear decay topology: an exit. 213016, 214017 and 219018 are specks 38-54 cm back off the body; 43003 and 43013 are delta rays on the body.

notes: FLAT_STOP: clean flat ~5e4 profile, charge ends in all planes mid-volume, nothing continues in 3-D; the track rises from the back face, so this end could be the start of a secondary rather than a stop
evidence: 101 cm single track; the chain entry is at the back face (z face 1.5 cm) low down at y=27, and the fit end is at (251.2, 93.9, 423.8): d_face 38.5 cm (z), 86 cm above the bottom, 107 cm from the anode, 249 cm from the cathode, 193 cm from the APA seam, in APA3. Not isochronous (|dx|/L = 0.56). The profile is flat and clean at ~4.5-6e4 over the whole visible window with no rise: one point at 7.4e4 at the very end, then 3.9-4.2e4 at 0.5-1 cm, and no climb over the last 20 cm; APA3 has no known deficit and there are no zero runs. Rule 3 holds: in f_meas (stop = high-time end, ~slice 968) U, V and W charge all end there; the only dead band (W ~9535) is ~145 channels away; the end is not at a face, the anode, the cathode or the seam; the three azimuths show nothing continuing past the star and the table holds no other object at all (no other-flash blobs reported). So a flat-profile stop: STM_ONLY with no decay activity and no capture gamma. Hard because the geometry runs upward (y 27 -> 94) from the back face, which is not how a cosmic muon arrives; the competing reading is a secondary that starts at this mid-volume point and exits through the back face, in which case this end is a start, not a stop.

notes: ANODE: fit end at face.x 7.1 cm, flat profile ending below plateau after a small bump; REVERSED: the lower chain entry end (y=223, 18 cm from the back face) is the real stop candidate
evidence: 333 cm straight track whose fit end is at (350.9, 446.2, 346.4), face.x 7.1 cm, i.e. |x| = 351 at the anode wire plane of APA3 (x>0, z>232); the chain entry end is at (145.3, 223.2, 443.9), 223 cm lower and 18 cm from the back face. The dQ/dx sits on a ~4-6e4 plateau; a 5-point bump to 0.7-1.06e5 at s=3-7 is followed by the last 3 cm back at 3.2-4.5e4, below the plateau, so the profile does not climb to the end along the muon curve: no clear rise, and no decay topology (nothing leaves the end in the three azimuths; 116004 straight ahead at 2-4 cm has no charge value, a degenerate row). The fit end is the upper end of the track, so a downward cosmic came in through the anode here and ran down to the lower end. f_meas shows clean charge to the end in all planes; the W dead band at ch ~9535 crosses the body 30 cm back, not the end. 117003 (3.6 cm at 30 cm back, on the body) is a delta ray: delta / other.

notes: ANODE: face.x 6.7 cm (|x| 351.3), profile falls toward the end; geometry is an anode entry for a downgoing muon exiting the front face
evidence: 53 cm; the chain entry is at the front face (z face 1.7 cm, y=418) and the fit end is at (-351.3, 460.0, 20.5): face.x 6.7 cm, i.e. |x| = 351.3, at the x<0 anode wire plane, 20 cm from the front face, in APA0. Not isochronous (|dx|/L = 0.25). The end sits 42 cm higher than the front-face end, so this reads as a downgoing muon that enters through the anode here and leaves through the front face. The APA0 profile is ragged (2.5-7.5e4 with dips to near zero at 29 and 40 cm), and toward the end it falls rather than rises: 2.5-4.5e4 over 4-8 cm and 0.5-1.5e4 over the last 3 cm. No rise at the anode end. No decay topology: 25004 is a 2.9 cm stub straight on (cos_fwd 0.95, 0.4 cm off axis) at ~1.0e4, a continuation into the anode, tagged muon as a THRU stub with charge; 24005 is a degenerate row (no dQ/dx): delta / other. All three azimuths show nothing else at the end. f_meas: U, V and W charge end at the low-time end (~slice 810, shortest drift), no dead band nearby. An end at the anode with no rise: THRU.

notes: Near-isochronous (x within 4 cm over 30 cm) with the end on a W dead band edge and a flat half-MIP profile; rule 3 excluded. Competing reading STM_ONLY from U/V charge ending.
evidence: 30 cm faint track; enters through the top (y=605.8, 0.2 cm) and the fit ends at (-345.6,581,275) in APA2, 24.7 cm below the top, 12.4 cm from the -x anode face, 44 cm from the APA seam and 343 cm from the cathode. It is near-isochronous: x runs only -349.4 to -345.6 over 30 cm (local x-component ~0.15), and the whole track sits in ~17 time slices (605-622) in f_meas, with only 92 image points. The dQ/dx profile is smooth and low, 1.5-3e4 along the whole length (about half the muon reference plateau), with a gentle wave and no climb at all over the last 20 cm; the smoothness and sparse imaging say this profile is poorly measured. The object table holds only the two fitted segments; nothing is drawn past the end in any azimuth, no arm, stub or speck. f_meas: the stop end sits right at the edge of a W dead band (ch ~8888), so the collection plane cannot say whether charge continues; U (which has a dead band mid-track at ch ~2085) and V show the track ending there with nothing beyond in the window. Rule 3 does not apply to a near-isochronous track, there is no rise and no decay topology, and the end coincides with a W dead band, so the reading is a track whose continuation is lost, not a stopper. Hard: U and V both show the charge ending, which on a non-isochronous track would make this a FLAT_STOP; a 100 MeV stopper entering from the top is also plausible.

notes: Near-isochronous top-to-back-face crosser; end 1.4 cm from the z=462 face. Medium only because of the isochronous clause; would otherwise be high.
evidence: 455 cm; enters through the top (y=604.8, 1.2 cm) at z=233 and the fit ends at (-55.4,286,460.9), 1.4 cm from the back face (z=462), 53 cm from the cathode and 230 cm from the APA seam, in APA2. The whole track is near-isochronous: x stays between -55 and -58 over 455 cm, and f_meas shows it as a horizontal line at slice ~380 across all three planes, crossing several U/W dead bands. The dQ/dx profile over the last 40 cm is smooth and wavy at 3-5e4 with a dip to ~0 at s=27 (an interpolation artefact of isochronous imaging), and it is flat at ~4.5e4 over the last 5 cm with no climb along the muon curve. Nothing sits past the end: the only non-chain row is 33012, a 1.7 cm pdg-11 speck at the top entry point 392 cm back (delta / other). In the stop azimuths the end is a clean track end with no arm; the dotted grey trace beside the track is the fit/image offset along the isochronous line, not a second object. The end is at a face with a flat profile, so this is a top-to-back-face crossing muon. Confidence is set to medium only because the rubric asks for medium/low on near-isochronous tracks; the exit itself is not in doubt to me.

notes: ANODE: fit end at face.x 6.4 cm, flat profile; the other end is on the front face, so the track crosses two faces
evidence: 37 cm corner-clipping track in APA0 (x<0, z<231) at y~507-518: the chain entry end is on the front face (z=0.7, 0.5 cm from it) and the fit end is at (-351.6, 507.0, 16.0), face.x 6.4 cm, i.e. |x| = 352 at the anode wire plane. Both ends are at faces. The dQ/dx is ragged (0.8-8e4, APA0 patchy collection) and the last few cm read 2-6.8e4 with no climb along the muon curve: no rise. Nothing leaves the fit end at an angle in the three azimuths; 47009 (3.2 cm, 1.5-2 cm out, no charge value) is a degenerate row. f_meas shows charge to the end in all three planes with no dead band there. A short track entering through the front face and leaving through the anode. The delta rays and the unassigned 202010 sit 16-22 cm back near the entry: delta / other.

notes: NO_MEASUREMENT: near-isochronous (x within 4 cm over 200 cm, parallel to V), APA0, smooth low profile with zeros; rule 3 excluded, only a collinear stub past the end. Leading alternative THRU (lost isochronous continuation), cf. owner isochronous THRU precedent.
evidence: 200 cm; the chain entry end is 3.9 cm above the bottom face (y=11.5, z=305) and the fit end is mid-volume at (-94.4,85,201) in APA0, 77 cm above the bottom, 30 cm from the APA seam, 92 cm from the cathode and 264 cm from the anode. The track is almost perfectly isochronous: x stays within -90 to -94 over 200 cm, f_meas draws it as a horizontal line at slice ~365-383, and it runs nearly parallel to the V wires, so V collapses it onto a few channels around 3500. The fit zig-zags in the 3-D views, a sign of isochronous imaging trouble. The dQ/dx profile is smooth and very low (0.5-3.5e4, a gap of zeros at s=9-11) with APA0 on top, so the last 20 cm carries no usable Bragg measurement. Past the end: only 53009, a 4.7 cm stub at 0-4 cm running straight on (cos_fwd 0.98, no kink), weak topology that I tag as muon continuation. 249007 is a 3.9 cm faint piece 44-48 cm back, ~22 cm off the body line, inside a sparse cloud of thinned context points (delta / other); 53006 is an attached arm 75-83 cm back on the body (delta / other). A large grey isochronous band of context charge at the same x crosses the detector ~235 cm above the stop. Rule 3 is excluded for a near-isochronous track, there is no rise to read and no decay topology, so neither a stop nor an exit can be established. Leading alternative: THRU, since the fit end is the upper end of a bottom-entering isochronous track and a lost continuation is the usual isochronous failure.

notes: Competing reading STM_MICHEL: muon stops at the kink ~10 cm back and the bent piece (dip then hot end) is the electron; no pin moved because the collapse precedes the peak rather than following it. 157001 gamma is a 2-point speck at 55 cm; its tag decides detached dots vs none.
evidence: 162 cm single segment; the chain entry end is near the top/-x anode corner (6.1 cm from the anode face, 10.4 cm below the top) and the fit end is mid-volume at (-264,466.5,292) in APA2, 94 cm from the anode, 139.5 cm below the top, 61 cm from the APA seam and 262 cm from the cathode. The last ~10 cm bends by roughly 30-40 deg away from the straight body (clear in all three stop azimuths). Profile: plateau ~5.5e4 over s=12-45 (single 7.7-8e4 points at s=19 and 31); a dip to 1.5-2.5e4 over s=4-11 in the bent section; then the last 3 cm climbs to 0.86-1.1e5, about 2x plateau, sitting right on the muon reference curve. f_meas shows why the dip is untrustworthy: the bent section runs at constant time (slice ~330-332) in U and W, a short near-isochronous piece, while V ends cleanly at the same slice; the charge ends in all three planes at the fit end with no dead band there and nothing continuing in the window. I read the end as the muon Bragg peak after a low-momentum end-of-range bend, with the dip an imaging artefact of the isochronous piece (sub-MIP charge is unphysical for either a muon or an electron). Nothing is drawn past the end: no stub or hot tip ahead (no undershoot). One 2-point, 0.4 cm speck 157001 sits 55 cm out at cos -0.82 but ~32 cm off the body line: isolated and inside 60 cm, so a capture gamma on an STM_ONLY. Hard: the bent 10 cm could instead be a Michel leaving a muon that stopped at the kink; I did not take that because there is no rise before the kink (s=11-20 is plateau) and the end shape follows the muon curve.

notes: Competing reading STM_MICHEL if 110011/110013 (branching off the body ~10 cm upstream, 10-16 cm from the stop, cos ~-1) are taken as a backward Michel arm; I read them as delta rays because they do not start at the stop vertex.

notes: ANODE: end at face.x 6.7 with no rise; the chain Michel pair (115040, 116015) is a ~3 cm low-charge hook at the wire plane, not clear topology; 115040 tagged muon as the straight-on continuation, 116015 delta / other

notes: Competing reading: a stopper with an unresolved Bragg peak (the 2-3 cm end spike) plus detached gammas 452033/451032 (kind detached dots). notes: Near-isochronous track with patchy APA0 W charge: the end position is unreliable. evidence: 301 cm, the chain entry is at (-0.5, 321, 43), i.e. at the cathode, and the fit end is the UPPER end at (-27, 534, 203) in APA0, 72 cm below the top face, 24.6 cm from the cathode and 28.5 cm from the APA seam. notes: 298015 is a 2-point, 0.1 cm speck (near-degenerate but has dqdx); tagged gamma, which with 296013/297014 decides both vs attached.

evidence: 73.6 cm straight track in APA2 (upper part, y ~553-606, not the bottom-corner hole region). notes: NO_MEASUREMENT: APA0 W charge missing along most of the track and dQ/dx near zero over the last 25 cm. evidence: 96 cm track in APA0, enters through the top near the anode (y 605.5, d_face 0.5), fit end at (-295.9, 545.8, 223.4): 60 cm below the top, 62 cm from the anode, 293 cm from the cathode. The dQ/dx rises from a low APA0 plateau of ~0.2-0.3e5 (s 15-40) to 0.6-0.75e5 at s 4-8, i.e. 2.5-3x its own plateau; two points dip at s 2-3 and the last point is back at 0.58e5, scatter rather than a sustained collapse, so no pin move. 18021 carries straight on 7 cm (cos_fwd 0.99) with charge falling from 0.55e5 to 0.15e5 as it goes out, not a hot tip. The decisive object is a ~40 cm near-isochronous pdg-11 branch (18016, 18017, 18018, with small far pieces 18013-18015 at 42-50 cm) whose pieces all sit at cos_fwd -0.78 to -0.81 at every distance from 10 to 50 cm, so it radiates from the stop at ~140 deg to the muon, well clear of the body (~6 cm off the line at its near end). In 3-D its imaged points start ~10 cm out, but in U and W of f_meas its horizontal (single-drift-time) line runs right up to the muon end cells, so I read the 3-D gap as isochronous imaging loss and the branch as attached at the stop: the electron.

notes: FLAT_STOP: APA0 wave profile, stop by rule 3; competing reading STM_ONLY, taking the 1.6 cm stub as the muon last centimetre (then all four specks would be capture gammas, kind detached dots); the Michel is very short for an electron, so michel vs muon on 20068 is the soft spot
evidence: 451 cm track (1 GeV by range) from the top face (y 605.4, d_face 0.6) down to (-228.8, 236.4, 42.6) in APA0: 42 cm from the front (z) face, 129 cm from the anode, 226 cm from the cathode and 188 cm from the seam, well inside. notes: seam 5.0 cm away in z (~9 cm along the track) and the rise rests on the last two points, hence medium; competing reading THRU across the seam with the continuation lost, rejected because nothing is imaged past the seam; 169008 called gamma (detached beyond 10 cm) although the chain types it the Michel
evidence: 52 cm track in APA0, enters through the top (y 605.6, d_face 0.4), fit end at (-245.7, 568.6, 226.0): 37 cm below the top, 112 cm from the anode, 243 cm from the cathode, and 5.0 cm from the APA seam in z; the track meets z at dz/ds ~0.58, so the seam lies ~9 cm further along the line, not at the end. notes: UNDERSHOOT: minor, 1.8 cm; 119014 at ~1.7x plateau continues the Bragg level, tagged muon (true stop at its far end); the verdict does not depend on it since the lower-charge 119003/119004 carry the decay
evidence: 259 cm track that starts high in the x>0 volume (y 588.5, 17.5 cm below the top), crosses the cathode some 50 cm before its end, and stops at (-42.8, 377.1, 353.4) in APA2: 40 cm from the cathode in x, 109 cm from the back (z) face, 229 cm from the top/bottom and 122 cm from the seam, so contained and not at the cathode. A muon at its Bragg peak cannot continue at half-MIP, so this is a second particle leaving the stop: the Michel. f_meas shows the track ending with a short low-charge hook in V and W, no dead band. 364012 (25 cm) and the faint 362010 (57 cm) lie on the forward side: gamma. 363011 (27 cm) and 361009 (35 cm) sit behind the stop at cos_fwd -0.8, away from the electron: delta / other.

notes: Tag note: 379007 has size 0.0 (2 coincident points) but a real dqdx 1.07e5 and a centroid consistent with d_min 10.7; tagged delta / other under the literal size-0 degenerate-row clause. evidence: 42.8 cm track in APA3 (stop x=24.5, z=312.7). A dip to ~4e4 at s=2-3 recovers at the last points, so it is scatter, not a sustained collapse: pin left at the fit end. Hot-tip check fails: nothing lies a couple of cm straight ahead. 245.6 cm track entering through the top (4.8 cm from y=606) and stopping in APA2 (x=-82.3, z=267.9, y=499, so not the low-y APA2 corner), 106.8 cm from the nearest face, 79.8 cm from the cathode and 36.9 cm from the seam: mid-volume. Undershoot at most ~1 cm, not a hot tip, pin left. 42009/42014/42019 are the muon chain further up; 42011 (125 cm) and 42018 (212 cm) lie on the body far back: delta / other. f_meas: charge ends in all planes with the arm; a narrow W dead channel near the end is crossed, not swallowing it; the V horizontal line at slice ~62 is an isochronous other track.

notes: NO_MEASUREMENT: along-drift track in the APA2 bottom/far-z coverage-hole corner, last 20 cm has no live charge; DEAD: predicted band runs over empty measured cells; FACE: stop 9.3 cm from the bottom face. +21 blobs from another flash hidden.
evidence: 64 cm fit with only 20 chain points, running almost exactly along the drift axis (x -110 -> -48.5 at constant y~17, z~442), in the APA2 bottom far-z corner: the stop is 9.3 cm above the bottom face, 19.5 cm from the back face, 46 cm from the cathode. Every other row is a 2-point speck 18-54 cm out (the chain calls three of them capture gammas) or the degenerate 49001 (583 cm, no dqdx); with no identifiable stop they cannot be placed relative to one. No rise, no topology, and rule 3 fails (the end is in a coverage hole, near the bottom face).

notes: ISOCHRONOUS: whole track at x~346.7 in a few time slices, rule 3 exception; no rise at the fit end. notes: Competing reading MESSY (rule 6): 97006, a 12 cm cluster lying along the muon body at its end, splits the charge; I judged the stop vertex and the branch leaving it isolatable from the f_meas V-kink. evidence: 243 cm track entering through the top (6.7 cm from y=606) and ending in APA1 (x=196.5, z=218.6, y=434) 161.5 cm from the nearest face, 194 cm from the cathode and 12.4 cm from the APA seam (not a seam crossing at that distance). Its first ~7 cm read low (0.8-2.3e4) and the far branches ~4.6-5.1e4: an electron, not a muon at its peak continuing. 97006 is a 12 cm strand running parallel on the muon body from 2.3 to 13.6 cm back (cos_fwd -0.97), branching off the muon 2.7 cm before the stop, not at it: hugging the body, delta / other; it doubles the track at the end and likely explains the fit dip. 361017, a 2-pt speck 42 cm out forward and on the Michel side of the stop: gamma. 97015 at 113 cm on the body: delta / other. notes: DEAD: the last ~12 cm of the fit carry near-zero charge after a flat MIP plateau (charge void, not a collapse after a peak); rule 3 fails because a hole swallows the end. Competing reading UNCLEAR / NO_MEASUREMENT. Physically the fit end is the upper end of a downward track, so the likely entry; the lower end is at the bottom face and the cathode.
evidence: 494 cm track. The chain entry is at the bottom face right at the cathode (x=0.6, y=9.3, face.y 1.7); the fit end is mid-volume in APA3 (x=64.3, y=450.5, z=324.7), 137.6 cm from the nearest face, 61.8 cm from the cathode, 93.7 cm from the seam. The muon is at MIP exactly where its charge disappears, which a stopping muon cannot be; it reads as the track losing its imaged charge (the grey imaged cloud thins and the fit points go blue toward the star in c/d/e), i.e. a flat profile running into a hole. The last fitted piece 109013 (0-5.1 cm, cos_fwd 0.99, 8.7e3) is a small hook at the very end, straight on, no kink, no charge: not decay topology. Nothing else lies past the end; the four delta / other rows are 150-414 cm back on the body. The direction supports it: a downward cosmic makes this upper end its entry into the cluster, and the lower end sits on the bottom face at the cathode. Hard part: no face, seam or cathode at the end, and f_meas cannot show a continuation in another cluster.

notes: ANODE: stop face.x 5.9 cm (|x|=352.1), flat profile fading to ~1e4. The chain Michel 421020 is a detached 2-pt speck 11.6 cm out.

evidence: 277.3 cm track. The chain entry is on the bottom face (y=9.8, face.y 2.2); the fit end is its upper end at x=-176.7, y=228.7, z=229.4, which is 1.6 cm from the APA seam, in APA0 (x<0, z<231), 181 cm from the anode face and 174 cm from the cathode. The profile is APA0-patchy: it oscillates between ~0 and ~5e4 with periodic zeros (s=25-30, s=42), a local bump to 6-7.7e4 at s=4-11, and then drops to ~0.3-3e4 over the last 3 cm. Nothing electron-like leaves the fit end in c/d/e: the long pdg-11 object 34047 (52.7 cm, 1.2e4) with its shower pieces 34048/34049 branches off the muon body about 20 cm back from the star and runs away at an angle (it only projects onto the muon line in the d azimuth); it does not start at the stop, and the f_meas horizontal branch near slice 1265 in U/W is that object. evidence: 166.8 cm track entering through the top (0.4 cm from y=606) and stopping in APA0 at x=-317.0, y=466.7, z=73.6: 41 cm from the anode face by the numbers (|x|=317, ~35 cm inside the wire plane, not the anode band), 73 cm from the front face, 157 cm from the seam, 314 cm from the cathode: mid-volume. notes: ANODE: fit end at face.x 5.9 cm (|x|=352.0), flat APA0 profile; other end 1.0 cm from the bottom face

notes: NO_MEASUREMENT: 3 fit points in the last 20 cm, no plateau, U/V show no measured track; FACE: fit end 4.8 cm from the bottom face; DEAD: the whole chain lies in the APA2 bottom far-z coverage-hole corner

notes: ISOCHRONOUS: constant x, horizontal line in U/V, one W channel; FACE: fit end 0.4 cm from the back z face, entry 0.1 cm from it

notes: NO_MEASUREMENT: segment mean 982 e/cm, no measured charge along the fit in any plane; DEAD: APA2 bottom far-z coverage hole; ISOCHRONOUS: x changes 3.5 cm over 116 cm; FACE: fit end 4.1 cm from the back z face

notes: NO_MEASUREMENT: 15 cm object with sub-MIP charge and no plateau, no identifiable muon body; possibly a fragment of an object clustered elsewhere (one other-flash blob hidden)

158 cm chain entirely in APA0. The fit end is mid-volume at (-256,323,160): d_face 102 cm (anode side), 253 cm from the cathode, 71 cm from the APA seam, 283 cm from the top. notes: FLAT_STOP: only a weak 3-point rise at the tip in patchy APA0 charge; charge ends in all planes mid-volume, 52 cm from the cathode and 39 cm from the seam; alternative STM_MICHEL if 36020 (backward arm from a vertex 8.75 cm back) is the Michel

notes: FLAT_STOP: APA0 patchy wave, no rise; charge ends in all planes mid-volume; the fit end is the upper end of the track, so a stop requires an upward-going muon; alternative reading THRU with the upstream body lost (APA0 or another cluster)
evidence: 190 cm straight track in APA0 whose chain entry is at the cathode (x=-1.8, y=333, z=65; the track crosses into the x>0 volume there, continuation in another cluster) and whose fit end is mid-volume and UP-track at (-52.1,452.2,158.3): d_face 154 cm (top), 50 cm from the cathode, 73 cm from the seam, 306 cm from the anode. The dQ/dx is the APA0 patchy wave, 5-40k with no plateau level to speak of and no rise at the end (last point ~27k after a dip to ~5k at s 2). f_meas shows the charge ending at the fit end (the earliest time slice, t~1210) in U, V and W with no dead band there, and the three 3-D azimuths show nothing beyond the star; no object in the table starts at the stop (the three delta rows sit 51-80 cm back on the body line). So all four rule-3 tests pass and the rubric calls it a stop. Why low: the fit end is the UPPER end of the track (y 452 vs 333 at the cathode), so a stop here means a muon travelling upward from the cathode, which is rare for a cosmic; the more natural reading is a downward cosmic whose upper part (above y=452) was lost, either in APA0 patchy collection charge or to another cluster/flash (two other-flash blobs are hidden). No measurement near the end can separate the two.

notes: ANODE: fit end at face.x 5.9 cm (|x|=352.0); the last two points (85k, 122k) are a terminal spike after a sub-plateau dip, not a Bragg rise
evidence: 338 cm straight track entering through the top (0.8 cm from y=606) and ending at x=-352.0, face.x 5.9 cm, i.e. at the anode wire plane, in APA2 at y=292, z=350 (mid-height, not the APA2 bottom corner), 118 cm from the seam. notes: ISOCHRONOUS: x changes 2.4 cm over 37 cm, ghost fan in 3-D; stop called on the perpendicular arm 80006 (rule 1) with no rise; 300007 michel vs gamma is an attachment call (decides attached vs both)
evidence: 37 cm track just under the top face in APA0: chain entry 3.4 cm below the top at (-112.5,602.6,53.8), fit end at (-114.9,594.3,25.9), 11.7 cm below the top and 25.7 cm from the front z face, 112 cm from the cathode. x changes by only 2.4 cm over 37 cm, so it is near-isochronous: all three f_meas planes show it as a horizontal band at t 325-335 and the 3-D frames carry a wide fan of grey ghost points around it. The dQ/dx is APA0-low and falls toward the end (35-75k at s 22-35, 15-35k over the last 20 cm, ~20k at the end): no rise. At the stop, 80006 (10 cm, 11.6k, starting at the stop, cos_fwd 0.06) leaves roughly perpendicular to the muon in all three azimuths, an arm from the stop vertex; 300007 (4.7 cm, 9.4k, 6.7-8.6 cm out, cos_fwd 0.78) is a compact piece on the same (-z) side, close to the far end of 80006 in the d azimuth, taken as part of the decay (gamma if it is truly detached). By rule 1 the perpendicular arm makes it STM_MICHEL. notes: FLAT_STOP: rise at the end is indistinguishable from the APA0 periodic dQ/dx wave; stop from rule 3 (mid-volume, all planes end, nothing continues)
evidence: 55 cm chain running mostly along z (entry z=10, 9.8 cm inside the front face; stop at (-59,401,51)), stop 50.4 cm from the nearest face (z), 56.7 cm from the cathode, 180 cm from the APA seam, in APA0. The dQ/dx profile is a periodic wave with ~11 cm period (crests near s=5, 16, 28, 39; troughs 2-4e4), which is the APA0 patchy-collection pattern: the last 8 cm do climb to 1.1-1.6e5 above the muon curve, but the crest at s=28 is as high, so the terminal rise cannot be told from the wave. Last point ~8e4 after 1.15e5: an ordinary 1-2 cm dip, not a sustained collapse, pin left at the fit end. f_meas: stop is the earlier-time end (drift 293 vs 300 cm); this cluster charge ends cleanly in U, V and W at both ends, dead channels (U~820, W~7095) are far from the track. Nothing continues past the star in any 3-D azimuth, and no row lies past the stop: no positive cos_fwd, so no hot-tip undershoot. 18004 (33 cm, pdg 11) branches off a vertex on the muon body 17-34 cm back from the stop, attached to the body, not isolated, so delta / other rather than a capture gamma; 18003 (1.8 cm) and the low-charge 18005 stub sit at the entry end. Stop is decided by rule 3 (mid-volume, charge ends in all planes, nothing continues) even if the rise is read as wave; with no decay activity, STM_ONLY. Hard part: whether the end crest is a Bragg rise or one more APA0 wave crest.

notes: OVERSHOOT: pin moved by topology (90 deg kink at the 22002/22005 vertex), not by a charge collapse, dQ/dx is an unreadable APA0 wave; gamma on 122004 (2-pt speck, 51 cm) is what makes the kind both rather than attached
evidence: 80 cm chain running along -z at y~584 (far end at z=182, 21.5 cm below the top); stop at (-64,584,123), 22.4 cm from the top face, 61.5 cm from the cathode, 108 cm from the APA seam, in APA0. Topology decides: the body (22001, 22002) arrives along -z at a vertex B ~3-4 cm from the fit end, then an ~8.5 cm straight piece runs perpendicular to the body (in -y) from B through the fit end to C. The centroids say it: 22005 sits 2 cm on +y of the fit end and 22006 2.3 cm on -y, both perpendicular to the body direction, so the fit end is mid-way along one straight piece and the sharp kink is at B. Its dQ/dx is essentially unmeasured: ~1e4 at the end with a bump to ~1.8e4 at 7 cm and near-zero from 10 to 27 cm, roughly a tenth of a MIP plateau, so no Bragg reading is possible. The fit end is not an end: it is a junction of four or five prongs. A 205 cm track (33007, pdg 4) starts 3.6 cm from the stop and runs up and back to z~384 where an 85 cm piece (33004) carries on to z~441, y~257; a 21.7 cm arm (33009) leaves downward nearly straight ahead (cos_fwd 0.89), a 10.5 cm shower-typed piece (33002) leaves sideways, and a 3.6 cm high-charge stub (33008, 1.26e5) sits right at the junction. A large object starting at the stop and carrying on rules out a rule-3 stop. Busy junction, MESSY; every row delta / other.
