evidence: Short 32 cm zig-zag chain near the bottom of APA0 (x -56 to -59, z 36-48). Upper ("entry") end at y 33.4, 25.8 cm above the bottom face, i.e. mid-volume; fit end at (-59.0, 18.8, 35.9), 11.1 cm above the bottom face, 56 cm from the cathode, 195 cm from the seam, in APA0. dQ/dx climbs smoothly and almost monotonically from ~1e4 at the upper end to ~7.2e4 at the fit end, steepest over the last ~12 cm; in APA0 only the shape counts, and the shape climbs towards the fit end, not towards the upper end. f_meas: this clusters cells end at the fit end in U, V and W (slices ~1230-1250), no dead band there. Nothing sits past the stop in any of the three stop views; the nearest other object is the unfitted diffuse cluster C32 (27-60 cm, no dQ/dx, a broad sheet off to the side, a different object) and the pieces 460009/460016/460017 of another track 64-128 cm up: all delta/other. No electron-like activity, so STM_ONLY on the rise. Hard: the climb is suspiciously smooth (APA0 patchy charge can smooth into shapes), the object has no visible upstream (its upper end is mid-volume, so the muon above it is in another cluster or not a muon at all), and 32 cm is short.

notes: FLAT_STOP: rule 3 on an APA0 patchy-wave profile (no readable Bragg); end 13.4 cm from the nominal anode face, just outside the at-anode band.
evidence: 58 cm chain in APA0 near the anode; upper end at y 592 (13.8 cm below the top face), fit end at (-344.6, 547.8, 95.3): face.x 13.4 cm, i.e. about 7.5 cm inside the anode wire plane (outside the <=8 cm at-anode band), 58 cm from the top, 95 cm from the front face, 136 cm from the seam, 342 cm from the cathode. The track heads towards the anode only slowly (x changes ~0.14 cm per cm), so it would need ~50 cm more to reach it. dQ/dx is the APA0 patchy wave: humps of ~3.3e4 at 6 and 13 cm, 2.7e4 at the end, near-zero from 15 to 30 cm; there is no readable plateau, so neither a rise nor a flat profile can be claimed. Rule 3 instead: in f_meas this clusters charge ends at the fit end in U, V and W together (slice ~1160); the one dead W channel (7097) is crossed ~15 channels before the end, it does not swallow it; not at a face, cathode or seam; and nothing continues past the star in any of the three stop views, with no other object in the table except the 3 cm delta 24003 that sits 4-7 cm back on the body line (cos -0.97, not at the vertex): delta/other. So a stop with no decay activity. Hard: the stop evidence is geometric only, with an unreadable APA0 profile and an end fairly close to the anode.

notes: FACE: fit end 0.7 cm from the bottom and 1.7 cm from the back face; DEAD: APA2 bottom/far-z corner coverage holes, only isolated blobs imaged.
evidence: 232 cm chain running along the bottom/back edge of the detector almost parallel to the drift: from (x -53, y 13.8, z 451), 6.2 cm above the bottom face, to the fit end at (-276.5, 8.3, 460.6), 0.7 cm above the bottom face and 1.7 cm from the back face, 274 cm from the cathode, in the APA2 bottom/far-z corner. Only 82 chain points and 147 image points over 232 cm: the 3-D frames show a dashed line of separate small blobs, and f_meas shows only a handful of isolated cells, i.e. the coverage-hole pattern of that corner. dQ/dx is 1-2e4 near the end and ~1e4 at 20-25 cm, with nothing in between: no measurement, neither rise nor plateau. The fit end sits in the bottom/back corner of the active volume, so the track could simply leave there; nothing electron-like past it, only nine tiny specks (0.2-1.9 cm, 28-54 cm out, most back along the body). Called an exit at the face; all non-chain rows delta/other. Hard: essentially no charge information at all, and both ends hug the bottom face, so this may be a track grazing the corner whose image is mostly lost.

notes: Kind both rests on a 0.1 cm, 2-point speck (246004) 51 cm out; attached if it is dropped.
evidence: 110 cm chain; enters 11.3 cm below the top face (y 595) and stops at (-44.9, 530.1, 269.8), 76 cm from the nearest face (top), 42 cm from the cathode and 39 cm from the APA seam, in APA2 (upper part, not the bottom corner). dQ/dx: plateau ~5-6e4 with a dip to 3e4 at 15-17 cm, then climbs along the muon curve to ~1e5 at 3-6 cm and ~1.1e5 at 1-2 cm: a clear rise, peaking at the end (no overshoot). A 10 cm arm 57001 (0-7.8 cm, cos -0.09, 4.9e4) leaves the stop at ~90 deg, clearly kinked away in views c and e: an electron at plateau charge where the muon is at its Bragg peak, so a second particle: michel. 57003 (0-6.7 cm, cos 0.44, 1.1e4) also starts at the stop vertex, within 10 cm: michel. Specks: 246004 (51 cm, +x/+z, on the side the Michel points to): gamma; 247005 (43 cm) and 248006 (37 cm) lie roughly opposite / off in unrelated directions: delta/other. A single dead W channel (~8888) sits about a centimetre before the end, but the charge continues past it and stops with the Michel attached, so it does not hide the end.

notes: SEAM: fit end 1.1 cm from z=231, but with a rise and a kinked arm whose charge falls outward. Kind both rests on one 0.6 cm speck 41 cm out.
evidence: 110 cm chain; enters 8 cm below the top face (y 598) and stops at (61.2, 522.0, 229.9), 84 cm from the nearest face and 59 cm from the cathode, but only 1.1 cm from the APA seam, on the APA1 side, heading +z into APA3. dQ/dx: a steady plateau ~5.5-6.5e4 over 40 cm, then a sharp rise over the last ~1.5 cm to 7.7e4 and 9.7e4, on the steep part of the muon curve; short but a rise, so the seam rule for a flat profile does not apply. Topology decides anyway: a 17 cm arm 108001 (0-14.9 cm, cos 0.6, 5.4e4) leaves the stop with a clear kink in all three stop views and its charge falls as it goes out (6-8e4 near the stop, 0.5-3e4 at 12-15 cm): a muon crossing the seam would carry on straight, and one that stopped 15 cm later would peak at the far end, so this is the electron. Speck 298004 (41 cm, 0.6 cm, forward on the side the Michel points to, cos 0.6): gamma. 294003 is a degenerate row (size 0.0, 2 points, implausible dQ/dx): delta/other. No dead band at the end in f_meas; the clusters charge stops at slice ~770 in all planes.

notes: ANODE: fit end at |x| 351.8 cm (face.x 6.2) with no rise; the three high points at 4-6 cm are scatter, not a peak-then-collapse, since the charge runs on to the wire plane.
evidence: 193 cm chain; enters through the front face (z 1.0, 0.7 cm) and the fit ends at (351.8, 366.6, 147.1): face.x 6.2 cm, i.e. |x| 351.8 cm, right at the APA1 anode wire plane; 239 cm from the top/bottom and 84 cm from the seam. dQ/dx: plateau ~5-5.5e4 with a dip region at 18-32 cm, three scattered high points (7.8e4, 8.8e4, 1.16e5) at 4-6 cm, then 2.5-3.5e4 over the last 2 cm: no sustained rise, the end is below the plateau as tracks crossing the wire plane usually are. Nothing leaves the end: only 136011, a 0.6 cm straight-on stub (cos 0.98) carrying real charge, tagged muon. The 18 cm purple arm 136008 starts 17 cm back on the body (cos -0.89), not at the stop vertex, and in views c/d/e leaves the body mid-track: delta/other, as are the two pieces 127-136 cm back (136005, 136009). The charge in f_meas runs up to the end in all three planes with no dead band there. An anode crossing: exit.

notes: ISOCHRONOUS: body at constant x ~70 for ~250 cm, end region not. Backward arm (cos -0.93) is the Michel; competing reading: a muon hooking back ~160 deg and stopping at the arm tip. 139005 michel vs delta is a tag doubt.
evidence: 319 cm chain; enters 7.9 cm below the top face (y 598) and runs nearly vertically at constant x ~70 cm (the body sits on one time slice, ~800, in all three f_meas planes: near-isochronous), then its last ~20 cm bends to x 58 and it stops at (57.9, 332.7, 258.4), 204 cm from the nearest face, 55 cm from the cathode and 27 cm from the seam, in APA3. dQ/dx: ragged plateau ~5.5-6.5e4 with bumps to 8.4e4 (5 cm) and 8.8e4 (12 cm), the last 4 cm at 5.7-7.3e4: at best a weak rise, not a clear one. Topology: the 19 cm arm 139007 (0-15.6 cm, cos -0.93) starts at the stop vertex and runs back up beside the body, diverging from it by several cm in views d and e (closer in c); its charge is mostly 1-4e4, below the muon plateau, so it is not the muon carrying on at its Bragg peak: michel under the backward-arm rule. 139005 (1.8-8.3 cm, cos -0.93, 2.3e4) sits at the vertex overlapping the start of that arm: michel (could be delta if it is the bodys own charge). Nothing ahead of the stop; the charge ends there in U/V/W (a dead W band at ~9307 lies ~20 channels past the muon end, beside the arm). Hard: the arm is nearly anti-parallel to the muon (a hook), the profile has no clean rise, and the body is isochronous; the two far points of the arm at ~15 cm (4.8e4, 7.5e4) could also be read as a hooked muons own end.

notes: FLAT_STOP: rule 3 on an APA0 wave profile. Competing reading (pin not moved): a fit bridge at the 32003/32001 junction (~17 cm), with the low 17 cm segment 32001 as the Michel; not taken because the segment is near-collinear and the track shows similar low-charge stretches upstream. The small blob 5-9 cm beside the stop sits inside C36 and could be decay activity.
evidence: 95 cm chain in APA0; upper end at (x -85, y 174, z 15.5), 15 cm from the front face, fit end at (-104.8, 117.2, 51.8), 51.5 cm from the front face, 102 cm from the cathode and 179 cm from the seam. dQ/dx is wavy: 3-8.5e4 over 20-45 cm, a bump to 8.2e4 at 22 cm, then the last ~17 cm (the final segment 32001, avg 2.5e4) stays low: near-zero at 10-13 cm, a 2.8e4 hump at 6 cm, 1.3-1.8e4 over the last 4 cm. No rise. I read the low tail as APA0 patchy collection, not a peak-then-collapse: the 22 cm bump is no higher than the earlier ones and the 43 cm upstream segment 32009 averages only 3.4e4 too, and 32001 continues the muon line with only a ~10-15 deg bend in the three stop views. Rule 3: this clusters cells end at the fit end in U/V/W (slice ~860), no dead band there, not at a face/cathode/seam, and nothing continues along the line: C36 (246 cm, unfitted) is a different track crossing ~9 cm away at another angle, including a small blob 5-9 cm off to the side of the stop: delta/other as a whole. So a stop with no attached electron. 129011 (3.9 cm, 28-31 cm out, off the muons extension in W/time) and 153012 (1.7 cm, 51 cm, well clear of the body): compact isolated pieces within 60 cm, capture gammas. C45 (83 cm, 50-60 cm) another object, 32007/32010 body deltas: delta/other.

notes: FLAT_STOP: rule 3 with only a one-point end rise after a hole. Competing readings: 151039 at 5.4 cm is the Michel (STM_MICHEL/attached), or the pin belongs at ~10 cm with the last piece as the far detached part. Kind hinges on 151039.
evidence: 471 cm chain; enters through the front face (z 8.2, 7.9 cm) and stops at (-160.7, 347.3, 388.8), 73.5 cm from the back face, 158 cm from both the cathode and the seam, in APA2 at mid height (not the bottom corner). dQ/dx: plateau ~4-5.5e4 (a delta-like bump to 1.25e5 at 29-37 cm), a small rise to ~7e4 at 14 cm, then a smooth V: down to ~5e3 at 6-8 cm and back up to 4.7e4 at 0.5 cm and 8e4 at the fit end. The 3-D stop views show a ~3 cm gap in the last segment 43001 just before the star, so I read the V as an imaging hole on the muons own line (43001 is collinear), not a fit bridge past the true stop: such a bridge would not end back at high charge. Rule 3 then holds: the clusters U/V/W cells stop at the fit end (slice ~745), no dead band there, mid-volume, nothing continues past the star. The only object past the stop is 151039 (2.7 cm, 6 points, 6e3, 5.4-7.2 cm out at 90 deg, cos -0.04), separated from the star by a clear gap in views c and e: by the attachment tie-break a detached compact piece, so gamma (capture gamma on an STM_ONLY). Pieces 80-360 cm back along the body (43009/43012/43017/43023 and the pdg-11 fragments 43025/43031/43034/43035 around 284-312 cm): delta/other. Hard: weak end rise through a hole, and 151039 sits right at the ~5 cm boundary of the Michel-across-a-gap rule.

notes: FACE: fit end 3.9 cm above the bottom face, track runs along the bottom edge from the anode; DEAD: APA2 bottom/far-z coverage holes; collinear pieces 185016/186017 ahead are probably the continuation.
evidence: 254 cm chain running along the bottom/back edge of APA2 almost parallel to the drift: from the anode (x -351.2, face.x 6.8 cm, y 13.1, z 447) to the fit end at (-114.3, 11.5, 448.6), 3.9 cm above the bottom face, 13.7 cm from the back face and 112 cm from the cathode. Only 122 chain points and 229 image points over 254 cm: a dashed line of small blobs with gaps, and in f_meas a few isolated cells per plane, i.e. the APA2 bottom/far-z coverage-hole pattern. dQ/dx is 0-1.5e4 everywhere with gaps; no measurement, neither a rise nor a plateau. Two small pieces (186017 at 40-41 cm and 185016 at 52 cm, cos 0.95-0.97) lie straight ahead on the same line at the same height, so the track most likely carries on along the bottom edge past the fit end through the holes; they are separate clusters, not chain segments, so tagged delta/other under the THRU rule. With the entry at the anode, the end 3.9 cm above the bottom face and charge continuing ahead, this is a grazing through-going track. 187018 (0.9 cm, 20 cm out, off to the side) and the other specks: delta/other. Hard: almost no charge information, so the call rests on the geometry and the collinear pieces ahead.

notes: ANODE: end at |x| 352.0 (face.x 5.9), flat profile, straight-on 1.2 cm stub only
evidence: 41.8 cm track entering through the top (y face 0.2 cm) and ending at x = -352.0 in APA2 (z 353), face.x 5.9 cm, i.e. at the anode wire plane; 36 cm from the top, 122 cm from the APA seam, 350 cm from the cathode. The dQ/dx profile has no Bragg rise: it wanders on a ragged plateau of ~4-7e4 with one hot cluster ~18 cm back, and the last ~6 cm dip low (a few points near 1-4e4) rather than climbing. f_meas shows the charge running up to the fit end in all three planes, no dead band at the end. The only other object is 53001, a 1.2 cm, 3-point fitted stub continuing straight on (cos_fwd 0.96) at low charge at the anode itself - muon continuation, not a kink or separate particle. Nothing else in the 3-D frames near the stop. Flat end at the anode face = exit.

notes: FLAT_STOP: rule 3 conditions hold formally (charge ends in all planes, mid-volume, nothing continues in 3-D) but the profile is an APA2 coverage-hole wave (NO_MEASUREMENT territory) and the fit end is the upper end of a track whose other end is at the bottom face; competing reading UNCLEAR / bottom-face THRU of a track starting here. The six far blobs as gammas are uncertain; they may be pieces of one faint object.
evidence: 55 cm track whose chain entry is at the BOTTOM face (y 7.9, face.y 0.3) and whose fit end is higher, at (-29.5, 38.8, 384.4) in APA2, in its bottom corner (y < 60): 31 cm from the bottom face, 27 cm from the cathode, 153 cm from the APA seam, 328 cm from the anode. The dQ/dx profile is not readable: it is a periodic wave between plateau-like peaks (~6-7.5e4) and dips to ~1e4 at s ~ 0-2, 11-12, 15-21 and 31 cm - the APA2 bottom-corner coverage-hole pattern - and the last ~3 cm sit in a dip, so there is neither a rise nor a readable collapse. f_meas shows this clusters own charge ending at the fit end in U, V and W with no dead band there (the U dead bands at 2035/2085 are far off). In all three 3-D azimuths nothing continues past the star; the imaged cloud ends there. No decay arm or piece within 40 cm. Six tiny compact blobs (0.1-2.5 cm, low charge) sit 41-60 cm forward (cos_fwd 0.4-0.7, higher z), well clear of the body line: capture-gamma candidates on an STM_ONLY, except 217006 at d_min 60.25, just past the 60.0 cm edge. What makes this hard: the profile carries no information, and the fit end is the UPPER end of the track, so a stop there needs an upward-going particle entering from the bottom; the alternative is that this end is where a downward track starts (produced by a neutral, or with its upstream part in a cluster/flash not drawn - 2 other-flash blobs are hidden) and the object is a bottom-face exit.

notes: ISOCHRONOUS: dx 8 cm over 294 cm, capped at medium. Competing reading STM_ONLY: 65003 is only a 1.4 cm fit stub overlapping the muons last cm, not a second particle; then 219001 would be a capture gamma (detached dots). Stop reading itself is supported by the rise.
evidence: 294 cm track entering through the top (face.y 5.3) and stopping mid-volume at (-128.9, 350.1, 329.0) in APA2 (not its bottom corner): 133 cm from the nearest face, 126 cm from the cathode, 98 cm from the APA seam. The track is near-isochronous: x changes only 8 cm over 294 cm, the whole track sits in ~30 time slices in f_meas, and the 3-D frames show a wide fan of imaged charge beside the body (isochronous imaging smear). The profile has a wavy plateau ~5-7e4 with dips, and over the last ~7 cm it climbs along the muon reference curve to ~8.7e4 at s ~ 4 cm (about 1.4x plateau), then the last 2-3 points sit at ~6.5e4 - a ragged but real rise; the drop is not below plateau, so no overshoot. f_meas: U and W charge end cleanly at the fit end; in V the end coincides with a narrow dead band at ch ~4950, but U and W are live there. Nothing continues past the star in any 3-D azimuth. 65003 is a 3-point, 1.4 cm segment attached at the stop vertex running straight back along the body (cos_fwd -1.0) at plateau charge; by the v2 rule an arm from the stop vertex doubling back along the body is decay activity, so michel. 219001 is a 0.9 cm speck 45 cm out, perpendicular to the body (cos_fwd -0.03), not along the backward Michel direction: delta / other. Hard because the Michel is tiny and indistinguishable from the muons own last cm in the frames, and because isochronous ends are unreliable.

notes: SEAM: fit end 2.0 cm from the APA seam, track nearly parallel to the seam plane, flat/wavy profile; REVERSED: the chain entry end (18 cm below the top, 4 cm from the seam) shows a rise to ~1.6e5 and may be the real stop candidate; cannot be judged here. Competing reading: s~6 bump then drop is a peak-then-collapse stop.
evidence: 42.7 cm fragment-like track. The chain entry is at (91.5, 587.7, 236.0), 18 cm below the top face and 4 cm from the APA seam; the fit end is at (96.5, 549.1, 233.0), 2.0 cm from the APA seam (seam_z 2.0), 57 cm from the top, 94 cm from the cathode, on the APA3 side of the seam. The track runs almost parallel to the seam plane (z changes 3 cm over 43 cm) and at the fit end is sliding into the seam gap. In W the whole track spans only ~10 channels between two dead bands (9278 and 9305-9310), and the fit end sits against the 9278 band. The dQ/dx profile is a periodic wave (bumps to 9-10.5e4 at s ~ 6, 21, 29, 37 cm over a ~5-6e4 plateau); the s ~ 6 bump is one of those, not a Bragg rise, and the last 2 cm fall to ~3.8e4. No object near the stop: the five other rows are tiny specks 42-59 cm away (two of them size 0 with no dqdx), all delta / other on a THRU. Nothing continues past the star in the 3-D frames, but a continuation along the seam gap would be invisible. Flat end at the seam = gap crossing. Hard because the other (entry) end is not at a face and its last few points rise to 1.2-1.6e5, which could be a Bragg peak at that end.

notes: UNDERSHOOT: the hot 3.6 cm straight-on tip 40006 (~2x plateau, rising outward) is the muons Bragg peak; real stop ~3.5 cm past the fit end at the tips far end, where the 7.9 cm kinked Michel 40005 begins. Chain types 40006 as an unclassified arm and 40005 as an unassigned pdg-11 shower.
evidence: 189.5 cm track entering near the top (face.y 12.5) and stopping mid-volume at (-80.5, 434.5, 366.1) in APA2 (y 434, not its bottom corner): 96 cm from the nearest face, 78 cm from the cathode, 135 cm from the APA seam. The fitted muon profile sits on a wavy ~6e4 plateau with a bump to ~1e5 at s ~ 10, a two-point dip to ~3.5e4 at s ~ 3 and ~7.5e4 at the fit end. Past the fit end, 40006 (3.6 cm, 7 points, straight ahead, cos_fwd 0.91) carries 1.29e5 mean, and in the dQ/dx panel its points climb from 0.9e5 to 1.3e5 going outward - about twice the plateau and rising: the muons own Bragg peak, so the fit stops short and the real stop is at the far end of 40006, ~3.5 cm past the fit end. 40005 (7.9 cm, 14 points) starts exactly where 40006 ends (d_min 3.45) and leaves at an angle (cos_fwd 0.54, a clear hook in the c/e azimuths and in all three f_meas planes, where it runs ~25 slices along drift) at plateau charge (6.6e4): a muon at its Bragg peak cannot continue at MIP, so this is a second particle, and 8 cm is Michel range. No other objects near. In V the end sits beside a dead band at ch ~5597, but U and W are live and show the hook.

notes: Tag doubt: 289006 (56 cm back, ~5-7 cm off the body line) could be read as a capture gamma under the any-direction STM_ONLY rule; kind stays detached dots either way.
evidence: 276 cm curved track entering near the top (face.y 11.7) and stopping mid-volume at (69.8, 352.7, 404.3) in APA3: 58 cm from the nearest face (z), 67 cm from the cathode, 173 cm from the APA seam. Clean Bragg rise: the plateau sits at ~6e4, climbs to ~9-10e4 over the last ~8 cm and ends at 1.06e5 and 1.38e5 in the last 2 cm (the 1.7 cm end segment 123004 averages 1.73e5), tracking the muon reference curve; no collapse after the peak, so no overshoot, and nothing straight ahead past the fit end, so no undershoot. f_meas: charge ends cleanly at the fit end in U, V and W; the V dead band at ch 6240-6248 is ~25 channels away. No arm or piece attached at the stop. 290007 is a compact 2.4 cm speck 18 cm from the stop (cos_fwd 0.51), well clear of the body in the d and e azimuths and past the end in all three f_meas planes (time ~340 vs the end at ~298): a detached capture gamma on an STM_ONLY. 123003 is the chains 6 cm delta ray on the body 77 cm back. 289006 is a 2.2 cm speck 56 cm back along the body (cos_fwd -0.99), only ~5-7 cm off the body line (on the track in W, ~15-20 channels off in U and V): read as body-side activity, delta / other.

notes: NO_MEASUREMENT: APA0 smooth-wave profile over the last 20 cm, nothing to read; rule 3 fails because imaged charge continues ~10 cm straight on past the fit end in all three 3-D frames. Competing readings: STM (true stop ~10 cm past the fit end, fit short) vs a downward track whose upper part is weakly imaged/split (FRAG_THRU). 191014 would be a capture gamma if this is a stopper.
evidence: 100.6 cm chain entering through the front face (z 2.4, face.z 2.2) at y 364 and ending higher, at (-101.9, 432.6, 42.1) in APA0: 42 cm from the front face, 99 cm from the cathode, 189 cm from the APA seam. The profile is the APA0 smooth wave: the last 20 cm decline smoothly from ~4.2e4 to ~2.5e4 with no point-to-point scatter at all (interpolated, weak collection plane), a single broad hump at s ~ 26, and nothing to read at the end - no rise, but not a readable flat plateau either. In all three 3-D azimuths a diffuse trail of grey (context) imaged charge continues ~8-11 cm past the star, roughly straight on along the track direction, with no fitted row for it; so rule 3 fails (something continues past the fit end) and the fit end is not established as the true end. No decay arm at the fit end. 191014 is a compact 2 cm speck 29 cm out (cos_fwd 0.74), clear of the body. A busy vertex region 43-55 cm back on the body carries short arms (35003, 35006, 35009, 189013). 379016/018/020/021 form a separate 100 cm track 51-78 cm away. Hard because the fit end is also the upper end of a track that enters from the front face, so a stop there would need an upward-going particle, while the straight-on continuation fits a downward track whose upper part is weakly imaged.

notes: FACE: fit end 8.4 cm below the top face, flat profile; this is the top entry of a downward 8 m through-going muon whose chain direction is reversed (chain entry at the front face z 1.2). Only doubt: 8.4 cm is a little more than the usual ~0 cm top-entry distance.
evidence: 802 cm muon crossing the detector from the top to the front-bottom corner: the chain calls the front-face end (329.8, 22.6, 1.4; face.z 1.2) its entry, and its fit end is the UPPER end at (124.8, 597.6, 335.9), 8.4 cm below the top face (y 606), in APA3, 122 cm from the cathode and 105 cm from the APA seam. The chain direction is reversed relative to a downward cosmic: the fit end is where the muon came in through the top. The profile over the last 40 cm is a flat ragged plateau of ~5-6e4 with a few low points near 4e4 at s ~ 3, no rise at all toward the fit end. f_meas shows the charge running straight to the fit end in all planes with no dead band there. Nothing leaves the end in any 3-D azimuth; the only nearby rows are two tiny specks 43 and 53 cm away (346037, 345036). The remaining rows are delta rays, unclassified arms and two small pdg-11 pieces 345-590 cm back along the body. A flat profile at the top face on a detector-crossing track is an entry, not a stop.

notes: UNDERSHOOT: only 0.6 cm - the hot straight-on stub 115006 (~1.5e5) is the muons last few mm, tagged muon; real stop at its far end. Tag doubt: the chain body-excluded 360003/361004/363005; at 10-18 cm off the body line I read them as clear of it (gamma); if read as body activity the kind becomes none.
evidence: 39.4 cm track entering through the top (face.y 4.5) and stopping at (16.7, 573.0, 403.8) in APA3, 33 cm below the top face, 14.2 cm from the cathode (not a cathode crossing distance), 173 cm from the APA seam. Clear Bragg rise: the plateau at ~5-7e4 climbs over the last ~3 cm to 0.85e5, 1.0e5 and 1.2e5 along the muon reference curve, and the 0.6 cm straight-on 2-point stub 115006 (cos_fwd 0.96) carries ~1.5e5, i.e. the muons own last few mm; no collapse after the peak. f_meas: charge ends at the fit end in U, V and W, no dead band there. Nothing leaves the stop in any 3-D azimuth; no piece within 18 cm. Three compact detached specks sit 18-33 cm away on the body side (360003 at 18 cm, ~10 cm off the body line; 361004 at 18 cm, ~16 cm off; 363005 at 33 cm, ~18 cm off): clear of the body line, so capture gammas on an STM_ONLY. 359002 is a degenerate 2-point row with no dqdx; 114001 is a separate 493 cm low-charge (7.5e3) vertical track sitting at the cathode plane, a different object.

notes: FLAT_STOP: flat profile at a mid-volume end where the charge ends in V and W and nothing continues in 3-D; the U end touches a dead band that may have hidden part of the Bragg peak. Competing reading: the straight-on 1.2 cm stub 116022 at plateau as a tiny forward Michel (STM_MICHEL); rule v2-11 treats it as weak, so muon.
evidence: 112 cm track entering at the top-back corner (face.z 0.4, face.y 1.2) and ending mid-volume at (266.7, 531.2, 407.4) in APA3: 55 cm from the back face, 75 cm below the top, ~85 cm from the anode wires (face.x 91), 264 cm from the cathode, 176 cm from the APA seam. The profile is flat: a ~5e4 plateau with a dip to 2.5-3.5e4 at s ~ 3-6 and ~5e4 at the fit end, no rise. The only piece at the end is 116022, a 3-point 1.2 cm stub straight on (cos_fwd 0.99) at plateau charge (~4.5-5.2e4): weak topology, read as the muons own last cm. f_meas: V and W charge ends cleanly at the fit end (time ~325); in U the end sits against a dead band at ch ~2597, but V and W are live there and show no continuation, so the band does not swallow the end. All three 3-D azimuths show nothing past the star beyond a ~2 cm wisp; no large object starts at the stop. Rule 3 holds: charge ends in the live planes mid-volume, far from any face, the cathode and the seam. Range (277 MeV) and MCS (243 MeV) agree, as for a stopper. 116017 is a 0.8 cm delta ray 60 cm back on the body.

notes: ISOCHRONOUS: the muon is near-isochronous (dx 1.9 cm over 45 cm), but the verdict rests on the rise plus a ~90 deg kinked arm running along drift, not on rule 3. Tag note: 128028 could alternatively be the muons last 4.8 cm (junction at the kink); its charge (~1-1.2x plateau) does not meet the hot-tip clause, so michel; the kind is attached either way.
evidence: 45 cm track entering near the top (face.y 11.4) and stopping at (72.2, 551.4, 381.6) in APA3: 55 cm below the top, 70 cm from the cathode, 151 cm from the APA seam, far from the anode. The muon is near-isochronous (x changes 1.9 cm over 45 cm; it sits at one time slice in U and V). The profile has a ~7-9e4 plateau and over the last ~8 cm climbs smoothly along the muon reference curve to 1.17e5 at the fit end: a clear rise. Past the end, 128028 (4.8 cm, straight on, cos_fwd 0.94) starts at ~0.98e5 and drops to 0.75-0.88e5 over its first 3 cm, i.e. back to plateau right after the muons 1.17e5 peak, rising again only at its far end where the arm kinks; that is not a hot tip at several times plateau, so it reads as the electrons start, not the muons last cm. At its far end the arm turns by roughly 90 deg (clear in the d and e azimuths and as a hook along drift in all three f_meas planes) into 128027 (9.6 cm) and 128020 (3 cm) at ~4.4-5.1e4, below the muon plateau - a muon at its Bragg peak cannot continue like that, so this ~17 cm kinked arm is a second particle, the Michel. No other objects. U has a dead band at ch ~2597-2600 by the hook, but V and W are live and show it.

notes: Pin not moved: the bump at s~9 followed by a ~0.65x dip over the last 2.5 cm could be read as an overshoot, but the dip is short and sits in a V dead band at the fit end; the backward-angled 12.5 cm Michel is attached at the fit end itself.
evidence: 83 cm track entering through the anode (x -352.0, face.x 6.0) and stopping at (-302.3, 192.4, 435.1) in APA2 (y 192, not its bottom corner): 27 cm from the back face, ~50 cm from the anode wires, 300 cm from the cathode, 204 cm from the APA seam. The profile sits at ~6e4, bumps to ~8.5e4 (1.4x plateau) at s 8-12, stays near plateau (6.3-7e4) at s 3-7 and falls to ~4-5e4 over the last ~2.5 cm. That last dip coincides with the V-plane dead band at ch ~4950 where the fit ends (U also has a band at ~2085 next to the end), so I read it as dead-band partial charge, not a sustained overshoot collapse, and leave the pin at the fit end. A 12.5 cm arm (19001, the chains Michel object) leaves the stop vertex at a clear angle - separate from the body line in all three 3-D azimuths, running up and back at roughly 30-40 deg to the muon (cos_fwd -0.81 measured on the local tangent) - at below-plateau charge (4.4e4 mean, with scatter up to 1.1e5): a second particle from the stop, the Michel. Nothing else near.

notes: Verdict hinges on 196008 at d_min 10.02 cm, right at the ~10 cm detached-piece edge with a visible gap: read as a detached gamma (STM_ONLY). Competing reading: STM_MICHEL with 196008 as a detached Michel fragment (kind both); the stop itself is not in doubt.
evidence: 147 cm track entering near the top (face.y 10.0) and stopping mid-volume at (-48.8, 509.3, 288.2) in APA2 (y 509, not its bottom corner): 97 cm below the top, 46 cm from the cathode, 57 cm from the APA seam. The profile sits on a ~6.5-7.5e4 plateau (a bump to ~0.88e5 at s ~ 6-7) and over the last ~3 cm climbs to 0.86, 0.96, 1.07 and 1.12e5, about 1.6x plateau, rising toward the reference curve: a Bragg rise, no collapse after it. f_meas: U and W charge ends at the fit end; nothing continues past the star in the 3-D frames. Nothing is attached at the stop. The chains Michel object 196008 is a compact 2.9 cm low-charge (2.4e4) piece 10.0-12.3 cm out, forward (cos_fwd 0.87), separated from the stop by a clean charge-free gap in all three azimuths (in W it sits by the dead band at ch 8888, but the gap between it and the track end is live): a detached dot at the ~10 cm edge, so gamma, not an electron from the stop. 192004 (31 cm, ~22 cm off the body line) and 194006 (47 cm, ~39 cm off) are compact detached specks: capture gammas in any direction on an STM_ONLY. 193005 and 195007 are degenerate size-0 rows with no dqdx.

notes: UNDERSHOOT: Bragg peak ~6-7 cm past the fit end inside 47010 (split row, tagged muon), real stop there; ISOCHRONOUS: whole object near-isochronous with a fan-shaped image smear, so the dQ/dx and the ends are unreliable - hence low. Competing readings: a corner-clipping through-goer from the top face (via 47007) to the back face with an isochronous charge spike mid-track (THRU), or MESSY (forked, smeared cloud).
evidence: A small object in the top-back corner of APA2. The fitted chain 47009 is only 17.4 cm: it enters 2.6 cm from the back face (z 459.7, y 577) and its fit end is at (-311.9, 589.6, 452.2), 10 cm from the back face and 16 cm below the top, far from the cathode and seam. The whole object is near-isochronous (x spans only ~7 cm over ~40 cm, ~25 time slices) and the 3-D frames show a broad fan of imaged charge under its far half. The fit end is not where the charge ends: 47010 (19 cm, fitted, chain-unclassified) carries straight on (cos_fwd 0.98) at the muons own charge, and its points climb from ~0.8e5 to a peak of ~1.6e5 about 6-7 cm past the fit end (about 2x the ~0.75e5 chain plateau), then fall steadily to 0.15-0.4e5 over the next ~8 cm - a peak-then-collapse inside one row. At 47010s far end two low-charge (~2e4) branches, 47006 (16.5 cm) and 47007 (9.9 cm), fork off toward the top face. I read this as the muons Bragg peak ~7 cm past the fit end (fit stops short) with the collapsed tail of 47010 plus the forked 47006/47007 as the Michel. 47010 is a split row: its first ~7 cm (muon, carrying the peak) and last ~9 cm (Michel start); tagged muon for the peak. 249008 is a 0.3 cm speck 18 cm out, roughly perpendicular to the Michel direction (+x): delta / other.

notes: NO_MEASUREMENT: APA0 weak collection plane leaves no W charge and the dQ/dx has no points over the last 20 cm; ISOCHRONOUS: x constant to 1.6 cm over 62 cm, so rule 3 cannot promote the flat end. Competing readings: an upward stopper ending 14 cm from the cathode (STM_ONLY) vs a downward track whose upstream is C119 or another cluster, exiting the bottom face (THRU).
evidence: 62 cm near-vertical track in APA0 whose chain entry is at the BOTTOM face (y 15.1, face.y 7.5) and whose fit end is its upper end, at (-16.6, 71.2, 66.9): 64 cm above the bottom, 67 cm from the front face, 164 cm from the APA seam, 14 cm from the cathode. It is near-isochronous (x -15.0 to -16.6 over 62 cm; a single time slice ~375 in U and V), and it sits in APA0, where the W row of f_meas shows essentially no measured charge for it. The dQ/dx panel has nothing to read: the last 20 cm have only a few zero-charge points at the end and no points at all from s 2 to 20, and beyond that a smooth low wave peaking at 2.7e4. In the d and e azimuths the track ends cleanly with nothing attached; the diagonal band that appears to cross the star in b and c is a projection of C119, a separate 212 cm unfitted track that passes 17 cm from the stop and runs across the cathode (faint diagonal line in the end and top views). A cluster of small pieces (416xxx, 417xxx, 415001) sits 35-62 cm away with its own diffuse cloud; C125 is a 1-point degenerate row. Hard: no charge measurement at all, isochronous ends are unreliable (rule 3 does not apply), and the fit end is the upper end of a track entering from the bottom, so a stop there needs an upward-going particle; C119 passing nearby is a candidate upstream for a downward reading.

notes: ISOCHRONOUS: whole object near-isochronous along the front face, dQ/dx carries no information; the fit end is a chain break, with the fitted 60 cm 93001 carrying the track straight on. Whether the full object stops at 93001s far end cannot be judged from these frames.
evidence: The fitted chain is a 38 cm middle piece of a longer near-isochronous track running along the front face in APA1: chain entry at (263.9, 231.9, 12.0), fit end at (267.6, 266.6, 14.1), 14 cm from the front face, ~85 cm from the anode wires, 265 cm from the cathode, 217 cm from the APA seam. x changes only ~4 cm along the whole object and everything sits in time slices ~1130-1160 in all three f_meas planes. The dQ/dx is unreadable: a smooth low wave (5e3 at the end, one hump to 4.5e4 at s ~ 17) with no scatter - isochronous imaging, not a profile. Decisive: 93001, a fitted 60 cm track in the same cluster, starts 2.6 cm from the fit end and carries straight on (cos_fwd 0.97) for another ~50 cm, clearly continuing the line in all three 3-D azimuths - far too long and straight for a Michel, so the muon does not stop at the fit end. Three tiny pieces at the junction (93018 1.8 cm, 93016 4.3 cm, 93017 1.2 cm, low charge) are clutter at the chain break. Behind the chain entry the line also continues (93021, 13 cm, on the body line 33-41 cm back), with small specks 296022 and 297023 (size 0) further back.

notes: Stop itself is high confidence (clear rise, mid-volume). Verdict STM_ONLY vs STM_MICHEL hinges on 330004 at 6.3 cm straight ahead behind a visible gap, faint; if read as the Michel this becomes STM_MICHEL/both.
evidence: 103.5 cm, enters 7.3 cm from the z=462 back face (35 cm below the top), stops 49.6 cm from the nearest face (z), 83 cm from the cathode and 182 cm from the APA seam, in APA3 (x=85.5, z=412.7). The profile sits on a ragged plateau of about 6-7e4 and climbs over the last ~5 cm to about 1.1e5 at the last point, following the muon reference curve: a clear Bragg rise. f_meas shows the cluster charge ending cleanly in U, V and W with no dead band at the stop. Past the stop the only nearby object is the chain Michel 330004, a 2.5 cm, 5-point speck at 6.3-8.0 cm straight ahead (cos_fwd 0.97) with very faint charge (~6.7e3, a tenth of the plateau); all three stop azimuths show a clean charge-free gap of ~6 cm between it and the stop, so by the attachment rule I read it as a detached dot (gamma), not an attached electron. Three further compact specks at 40-54 cm (327001 fwd-side, 328002 off to the side at x~110 away from the body, 329003 forward) are isolated and clear of the body line: capture gammas on an STM_ONLY. The hard part is 330004 alone: it sits between the 5 cm (Michel across a gap) and 10 cm (detached is gamma) marks.

157.6 cm, enters 0.9 cm from the z=462 back face at y=282, stops 76.4 cm from the nearest face (z), 221 cm from the cathode and 155 cm from the APA seam, in APA3 (x=223.6, z=385.9). The profile runs on a ragged plateau of ~6e4 and climbs in the last ~5 cm to ~1.2e5 and ~1.7e5 on the final two points, tracking the muon reference: a Bragg rise, no collapse, so the pin stays. At the stop vertex an arm leaves at a clear kink (~70-80 deg in all three azimuths): 110002 (11.8 cm, 1.8-7.5 cm out, cos_fwd 0.21) at about half the plateau with a diffuse, shower-like halo of image points, continuing into 110003 (16.2 cm, 7.5-14.9 cm, pdg 11 shower) and the short 110008 at its far end (13.8-14.9 cm). The chain is attached end-to-end from the stop and runs away from the body line: the Michel electron, total ~15 cm reach, right for a decay electron. The 4 cm, 84e3 piece 110004 is the fitted last muon segment at the Bragg peak. f_meas shows the muon charge ending in all three planes with no dead band at the stop; the horizontal line in V near slice 915 is an isochronous feature away from the stop.

notes: ANODE: face.x 6.2 cm; APA0 wavy profile, no rise; the chain Michel 34033 is a 1.6 cm speck on the body line.
evidence: 191.5 cm straight track, enters 1.2 cm from the z=0 front face at y=291 and runs up and out in -x to a fit end at x=-351.8, face.x 6.2 cm, i.e. at the APA0 anode wire plane (349 cm from the cathode, 161 cm from the seam, 208 cm below the top). The profile is the APA0 pattern: a low plateau (~3-5e4) with a smooth periodic wave dipping to ~1-2e4, and the last ~10 cm show no climb, ending at ~4.5e4 against the reference; no Bragg rise. Nothing leaves the stop in the three azimuths; the only object there is the chain Michel 34033, a 4-point 1.6 cm speck at 0.1-1.1 cm running straight back along the body (cos_fwd -0.98), which is not a second particle and I tag delta / other. The remaining rows (35020, 35025, 35028, 35031, 35032) are pieces 67-116 cm back along the body at cos_fwd -1: delta / other. f_meas shows the charge running to the end in all planes with nothing special there. Front-face entry to anode-face end with a flat, wavy profile: an anode exit.

notes: DEAD: end in the APA2 bottom far-z coverage hole, track along drift; THRU rests on colinear specks continuing to the cathode. Competing reading UNCLEAR/NO_MEASUREMENT.
evidence: 111.3 cm but only 42 chain points: the track runs almost purely along the drift direction (x -141 to -32) at y 12-15 cm, z 451-458, i.e. along the bottom edge in the APA2 bottom far-z corner. Entry at the back-bottom corner (z face 4.1, y face 7.1); the fit end is 4.1 cm above the bottom face, 11 cm from the back face, 29 cm from the cathode, in APA2 (x=-31.7, z=451.2). The dQ/dx panel shows only a few chain points in the last 30 cm, all at 1-2e4, far under any plateau (the body mean is 6.1e4 further back); in f_meas the fit runs vertically in time over a few wires with almost no measured charge in U, V or W, so the end sits in the documented APA2 coverage hole and nothing about a rise or a collapse can be read. Past the end, a string of small pieces lies straight on along the track line toward the cathode: 218002 at 10 cm (cos_fwd 0.90), 219003 at 19 cm (0.99) and 220004 at 31 cm at x=-0.5 (0.99). Colinear specks at increasing distance read as the continuation through the hole, not isotropic capture gammas or an electron, so I tag them muon. 217001 (14 cm, cos 0.37) and the pieces 27-47 cm back or off to the side are delta / other. No decay topology at the fit end. Hard because the whole end region is barely imaged: THRU rests on the colinear string, not on a flat profile.

notes: NO_MEASUREMENT: APA0 periodic wave, no plateau or rise to read; ISOCHRONOUS: dx 11 cm over 184 cm. Colinear pieces 19-28 cm past a gap suggest the fit stops short of the full object. Competing readings: FRAG_THRU (continues out, unimaged) or FRAG_STM_ONLY with the real stop ~28 cm further (UNDERSHOOT-like).
evidence: 183.6 cm, enters 19 cm from the z=0 front face near the top (y=559) and descends to a fit end at x=-42.6, y=450, z=107.4: 107 cm from the nearest face, 40 cm from the cathode and 124 cm from the APA seam, in APA0. The track is near-isochronous: x moves only 11 cm over 184 cm, and in f_meas the whole track lies in time slices ~50-90. The dQ/dx is the APA0 smooth periodic wave (0 to ~3e4, with a trough to near zero 8-13 cm from the end), with nothing to read as a plateau or a rise; W measured charge is patchy along the track. Past the fit end, three pieces the chain calls capture gammas (251012 at 19-23 cm, 250010 and 250011 at 25-28 cm, ~9 cm in total) lie straight on along the track line (cos_fwd 0.98-0.99) after a ~19 cm charge-free gap, at the same ~2e4 charge as the body; the c/d/e azimuths all put them on the extension of the track. Colinear pieces at plateau charge read as the muon continuing through an imaging gap rather than as isotropic gammas, so the fit end is probably not the stop; but where the full object ends (at ~28 cm, or beyond, unimaged) cannot be judged: isochronous imaging, APA0 charge, no rise, no decay topology. The 1.2 cm stub 57013 at the fit end runs straight on and is tagged muon.

86.2 cm, enters 14 cm below the top face (y=592) and stops at x=82.5, y=525, z=331.7: 80.6 cm from the nearest face (top), 80 cm from the cathode and 101 cm from the APA seam, in APA3. The profile runs on a smooth, slightly wavy plateau of ~3-5e4 and then climbs steadily over the last ~6 cm from ~2.5e4 to ~1.2e5 at the final points, following the shape of the muon reference curve: a clear Bragg rise, peaking at the last point, so no overshoot and the pin stays. The 3.2 cm last segment 88009 (1.05e5) is the fitted muon tip. Nothing leaves the stop in any of the three azimuths and the object table has no piece other than the muon chain; f_meas shows the cluster charge ending in U, V and W with no dead band near the stop. A separate straight track runs parallel to the muon some 30-40 cm off to the side in the 3-D frames (not in the object table); it is a different object and does not touch the stop. No decay activity, no capture gamma candidates.

notes: OVERSHOOT: ~3 cm collapse to 0.3-1.5e4 after a modest peak, inside segment 64018 (split row); could instead be charge sharing at a multi-arm vertex. Competing verdict MESSY (two arms plus a faint context track at the stop). 64023 (27.8 cm faint) as part of the Michel is the weakest tag.
evidence: 40 cm, near-horizontal along z at y~400, from 9.3 cm inside the z=0 front face to a fit end at x=-105.8, z=38.2: 37.9 cm from the nearest face (z), 103 cm from the cathode and 193 cm from the seam, in APA0. The profile is ragged around a ~5-8e4 plateau, rises modestly to ~8-10e4 between 4 and 10 cm from the end, then falls to 0.3-1.5e4 over the last ~3 cm (four to five points): a sustained collapse after the peak, inside the last muon segment 64018 (0-7.5 cm), so I move the pin to ~3.5 cm; the row is split (last ~3.5 cm electron-like, the rest muon) and tagged muon for its majority. Topology decides the stop: at the fit-end vertex the 16.6 cm arm 64027 leaves at ~90 deg (cos_fwd -0.10), wiggly, at about half the plateau: an electron. From the same vertex, via the 1.2 cm stub 64019, the faint pdg-11 pieces 64022 then 64023 (5.4 + 27.8 cm, ~1.5e4) run off at ~120 deg and separate from the body, and 64029 (6 cm, 4e3) runs back along the body; all attached at the stop, so tagged michel per the stop-vertex rule. 266030 (4.6 cm, 17-20 cm out, behind a gap, cos_fwd 0.01) sits on the same +x side as 64027, beyond its end: gamma. f_meas shows the cluster charge ending in all planes at the vertex, no dead band. Hard because the vertex is busy (two arms plus a faint straight context track 10-30 cm off, not in the table), so MESSY is the competing reading, and the pin move rests on only ~3 cm of low points.

notes: Tag doubt only: the six specks at 46-59 cm are near the top face and could be unrelated activity; 288006 and 285004 sit only ~10-16 cm off the body line.
evidence: 58.1 cm, enters through the top 0.8 cm from y=606 and runs almost straight down to a fit end at x=44.7, y=551.7, z=100.2: 54.3 cm below the top (nearest face), 42 cm from the cathode and 131 cm from the APA seam, in APA1. The profile sits on a ragged ~6-9e4 plateau and climbs at the end: ~1.0-1.27e5 at 6-8 cm, a two-point partial dip at 3-5 cm (near-zero points I ignore), then 0.98e5, 1.5e5 and 1.65e5 on the last 2 cm, on and above the muon reference: a Bragg rise peaking at the last point, so the pin stays. Nothing leaves the stop in the three azimuths and nothing sits within 45 cm; f_meas shows the charge ending in U, V and W with no dead band. Six compact 2-5-point specks lie 46-59 cm out, up near the top face and 10-30 cm off the body line (282001, 283002, 284003, 285004, 287005, 288006); isolated, clear of the body and within the 60 cm edge, they are capture-gamma candidates on an STM_ONLY in any direction. A long faint context track crosses the event far from the stop (x~140 at this z) and is unrelated.

notes: ISOCHRONOUS: whole object at slice ~800; the backward arm 30007/30008 forming a loop with the body could be an imaging ghost. Competing readings: MESSY or UNCLEAR. STM_MICHEL rests only on the stop-vertex backward-arm rule.
evidence: 16.2 cm near-vertical track, from 8.1 cm below the top (y=597.9) down to a fit end at x=-60.0, y=582.2, z=88.4: 23.8 cm below the top (nearest face), 57.5 cm from the cathode and 143 cm from the seam, in APA0. The track is fully isochronous: x is -60.0 at both ends and in f_meas all of its charge, arms included, sits in one horizontal band at time slice ~800-810 in U, V and W, so its imaging and its end are unreliable. The dQ/dx is high along the whole 16 cm (1.0-1.35e5, about 2x MIP), with a hump at 10 cm, a dip to ~0.9e5 at 4 cm and 1.25e5 at the end; with no plateau there is no rise to read. Topology: at the stop the 3 cm arm 30009 (cos_fwd 0.45, ~1e5) leaves the vertex and feeds the 10.5 cm arm 30007 (~4e4), which doubles back roughly parallel to the body, 3-5 cm off it, into 30008 near the far end, a thin V/loop in all three azimuths. Under the stop-vertex rule this backward arm is the Michel. 129012 (0.7 cm at 9.6 cm, detached, on the backward side) and 128011 (2-point speck at 14.6 cm, detached) are gammas; the 34 and 45 cm specks 127010 and 130013 lie forward, away from the Michel side: delta / other. Hard: on an isochronous track a parallel arm closing a loop with the body can be an imaging ghost or a delta ray, and the high charge along the whole track cannot confirm a stop.

notes: SEAM: 3.8 cm from z=231, flat profile, straight-on stub; ISOCHRONOUS: dx 7 cm over 236 cm. No drawn continuation past the seam.
evidence: 236.4 cm, runs along -z from 16.7 cm inside the z=462 back face (y=353) to a fit end at x=-206.8, y=400.8, z=234.8: 3.8 cm from the APA seam at z=231, 151 cm from the nearest face and 204 cm from the cathode, on the APA2 side of the seam. The track is near-isochronous (x changes 7 cm over 236 cm; in f_meas the whole track is one horizontal band at slice ~1435-1445 in all three planes, and the 3-D frames show the broad smeared fan of image points typical of isochronous imaging). The profile is flat and ragged around ~4-7e4 over the last 40 cm, with no climb at the end (last points ~6.5-7e4, under the muon reference). The 2.5 cm stub 36003 carries straight on past the fit end (cos_fwd 0.97) at plateau charge (6.7e4): the muon continuing, tagged muon. The only other row, 170001 (1.9 cm, 13.7 cm out, cos_fwd -0.62, 5e3), is a faint speck: delta / other. An end at the seam with a flat profile and a straight-on stub is the rubric gap crossing; no continuation is drawn beyond the seam in the APA0 volume, which on an isochronous track crossing into the weak-collection APA0 is expected, not evidence of a stop.

notes: SEAM: 2.4 cm from z=231, heading +z into it; ISOCHRONOUS: dx 3.6 cm over 54 cm; APA0 wave profile, no rise readable. No drawn continuation past the seam.
evidence: 54.2 cm, enters 14.9 cm below the top (y=591, z=205) and descends along +z to a fit end at x=-213.9, y=552.9, z=228.6: 2.4 cm short of the APA seam at z=231, 53 cm below the top (nearest face), 211 cm from the cathode, in APA0. The track is near-isochronous (x moves 3.6 cm over 54 cm; in f_meas it is one horizontal band at slice ~1415-1430 in all planes). The dQ/dx is the APA0 pattern, a smooth wave between ~0 and 4e4 with deep troughs, nothing that can be read as a plateau or a rise; the body dqdx is only 0.6-2.3e4. At the end the 0.6 cm stub 54009 continues straight on (cos_fwd 0.98) toward the seam: tagged muon. 54003 and 54007 (8-14 cm back, cos_fwd -1.0) lie on the body line: delta / other, as is the 2 cm speck 181008 40 cm off to the side. Nothing leaves the end at an angle, so there is no decay topology. An end at the seam, heading into it, on an isochronous track with no readable rise is the rubric gap crossing; no continuation is drawn on the APA2 side, which is why this is medium, not high.

notes: Michel vs STM_ONLY hinges on the two faint backward arms (0.6-0.9e4) that attach 3-4.5 cm back from the fit end; if read as body-hugging delta/other the verdict is STM_ONLY (FLAT_STOP not needed, there is a ragged rise).
evidence: 595.9 cm, enters 11 cm below the top near the back (x=-37, z=439), crosses the cathode mid-track and stops at x=30.9, y=177.7, z=124.3: 124 cm from the nearest face (z), 28 cm from the cathode, 107 cm from the seam, in APA1. The end is not at a face, the seam or the cathode crossing. The profile runs on a ragged ~6-8e4 plateau, climbs to ~1.0-1.1e5 at 10-12 cm, has a run of partial low points at 2-6 cm (1-5e4), and ends on ~0.8-1.07e5 on the last three points: a ragged rise to ~1.6x the plateau, peaking at the end, so no overshoot. f_meas shows the cluster charge ending in U and W (V is busy with vertex markers but no continuation), no dead band at the end; the 3-D frames show only the image-point halo ~5 cm past the star, no track carrying on. Two faint arms, 109031 (10.9 cm, from 3.2 cm) and 109027 (10.3 cm, from 4.5 cm), leave the body within ~4.5 cm of the stop and run backward in a narrow V (cos_fwd -0.95/-0.97), visibly separated below the body by a few cm in all three azimuths, at ~0.6-0.9e4. I take them as decay activity attached at the stop per the backward-arm rule. The specks 275036 (36 cm, sideways) and 276037 (52 cm, forward) lie away from the Michel side: delta / other; the arms 176-245 cm back along the body are delta / other.

notes: SEAM: 1.7 cm from z=231, track runs along the seam over its last ~70 cm; APA0 wave profile, no rise. If the two compact pieces at 9-12 cm were decay products this would become a stop with detached dots.
evidence: 553.8 cm, enters through the top 0.6 cm from y=606 at x=-271, z=196 and descends toward +x to a fit end at x=-20.9, y=205.7, z=229.3: 1.7 cm from the APA seam at z=231, 18.4 cm from the cathode, 198 cm from the nearest face, in APA0. Over the last ~70 cm the track runs almost parallel to the seam at z~226-229, so it sits in the seam coverage gap as it ends. The profile is the APA0 wave (troughs to ~1e4, crests to ~5-7e4) and the last 5 cm read only ~0.8-2.5e4, under any plateau: no rise, and little that can be read. Nothing leaves the fit end in the three azimuths and nothing continues in the drawn bundle (one blob of another flash is hidden). Nearby are two compact detached pieces, 161075 (0.3 cm at 9.2 cm) and 160074 (2.8 cm at 11.7 cm), both off to the side and behind the end (cos_fwd -0.65), plus specks at 36-53 cm and a degenerate row with no charge (34073); with no stop established they are delta / other. An end at the seam with no rise, on a track running along the seam gap and still heading toward the cathode, reads as a gap/coverage loss, not a stop; medium because the APA0 profile is barely readable and the continuation is not drawn.

notes: FACE: whole track in the z=462 back-face plane (0.2 cm), one W wire; DEAD: coverage holes along the fit, smooth-wave dQ/dx; grey trail continues ~10-15 cm past the fit end.
evidence: 107.3 cm, and the whole track lies in the z=462 back-face plane: the entry (x=-67, y=496) and the fit end (x=-25.0, y=401.6) are both 0.2-0.3 cm from the back face, the end 22.5 cm from the cathode and 204 cm from the top, in APA2. In f_meas the track sits on a single W wire (~9278) at the edge, with almost no measured W charge, while U and V carry it; the 3-D frames show coloured charge only in patches along the fit with grey undrawn stretches between, i.e. coverage holes along the boundary. The dQ/dx over the last 13 cm is a smooth wave (5.5e4 at the end, down to 2e4 at 9 cm, back up to 2.7e4), then a gap to 33 cm: no rise, and the smooth shape is the hole pattern, not a plateau. In all three stop azimuths a grey dotted trail carries on past the star along the track line for ~10-15 cm, so the object does not end at the fit end. The only other row, 68003 (3.9 cm, 85-88 cm back on the body), is delta / other. A track running along the back face through coverage holes with a trail continuing past the end is not a stop; medium because the end region has no readable charge.

notes: OVERSHOOT: pin moved ~26 cm (arc) to vertex A, a large move; rests on 119002 at half the body charge plus a 19 cm electron branch at A (too long for a delta at that residual range). Competing readings: stop at the fit end with a 2-point Bragg spike (STM_ONLY, 119006 then delta), or MESSY (busy curled end with an image-point sheet).
evidence: 70.6 cm, enters 9.7 cm inside the z=0 front face at y~208 and rises to a fit end at x=118.4, y=215.9, z=57.0: 56.8 cm from the nearest face (z), 116 cm from the cathode and 174 cm from the seam, in APA1, well inside. The body 119003 carries ~6-9e4 and reaches ~1.04e5 at s~29-30. At vertex A (arc ~26 cm, 12-14 cm straight from the fit end) the picture changes: the last fitted segment 119002 (26 cm of wiggly path to the star) averages only 3.2e4, about half the body, with a sustained near-zero stretch at s 17-24, ~plateau charge at s 5-13, partial points at 1-5 and a two-point spike (1.25-1.68e5) at the very end. From the same vertex a curly 19 cm pdg-11 branch 119006 loops off 5-8 cm clear of the body, with the small pieces 119005/119007, and a sheet of image points fills the region. A muon with only ~26 cm of residual range at A could throw a delta of at most ~2 MeV (under 1 cm), so a 19 cm electron there has to be decay activity: the muon stopped at A, and the fit overshoots through the electron. I move the pin to 26 cm and tag 119002, 119006, 119005 and 119007 michel. The 0.9 cm speck 338008 (52 cm, back toward the entry, off the Michel side) is delta / other. f_meas: charge ends in V and W; the U end sits against a dead band.

notes: NO_MEASUREMENT: whole chain at ~1e4 (APA0 plus isochronous imaging), no plateau; ISOCHRONOUS: x constant at -53. Competing readings: MESSY (EM fragments) or FRAG_THRU (broken isochronous track). The chain row may not be a muon at all.
evidence: 19.6 cm of chain that curls back on itself: the chain entry (x=-53.1, y=583.9, z=177.1) and the fit end (x=-53.6, y=587.4, z=173.7) are only ~5 cm apart, 18.6-22 cm below the top, 51 cm from the cathode and 57 cm from the seam, in APA0. The object is isochronous (x = -53 at both ends; in f_meas all of it sits at slices ~60-75, mostly vertex markers). The dQ/dx is ~0.5-2e4 along the whole chain (the fitted last segment 31003 reads 0.7e4, 31002 1.2e4), rising only to 3-5e4 at its far end: far below any muon plateau, with nothing to read as a rise or a collapse; the chain range-KE is 74 MeV but its dQ/dx-KE only 13 MeV. Around it, two groups of small curly pieces (207013/207014/207015 at 24-27 cm and 363017/363018/363019 at 31-35 cm, cos_fwd ~-0.8) and a grey trail leaving the chain far end sit at higher charge (2-5e4) than the chain itself; in one azimuth they roughly line up with the chain, in another they do not. I cannot tell whether this is the broken image of a near-isochronous track, an EM fragment, or a short stopper: no face, seam or cathode explains the end, but no stop evidence survives either.

notes: ISOCHRONOUS: x constant within ~4 cm over 177 cm; competing reading STM_ONLY (FLAT_STOP) since the end is mid-volume with nothing continuing; profile is a wave, not a readable Bragg shape.
evidence: 177 cm near-vertical track, entry 15.9 cm below the top face, fit end mid-volume in APA1 at x=66.5 (64 cm from the cathode, 197 cm from the APA seam, 33.7 cm from the z=0 face, 166 cm above the bottom). The track is near-isochronous: x runs only 62.9 to 67.3 cm over its whole length, and in f_meas it lies along a narrow band of time slices in U and V. The dQ/dx profile is a smooth periodic wave (peaks ~6.5e4 at s=24 and 38 cm, dips to near zero at s=12-17 and 31 cm) with no rise at the end: the last 10 cm sit at 2-5e4, below the wave peaks. The 3-D stop views show the fit zig-zagging between two parallel grey traces over the last ~20 cm, the ghosting typical of an isochronous image; nothing continues past the fit end and nothing leaves it. All four drawn rows are the fitted muon chain (86010 at the stop, 86009/86012/86011 back up the body). Hard because rule 3 would call a mid-volume end with charge ending a FLAT_STOP stopper, but the isochronous exception removes rule 3 and the end is untrustworthy; no Bragg rise and no decay topology, so I follow the owner precedent of THRU on a near-isochronous flat end, low.

notes: FLAT_STOP: mid-volume end, charge ends in all planes, nothing continues; Michel is only a straight-on 3.6 cm stub. Competing readings: STM_ONLY with 99001 as the muon tip, or OVERSHOOT with the true stop at the s~11 cm spike (rejected: the spike sits at a side-branch vertex and 0-10 cm is not below the wavy plateau). Track is moderately low-angle (x 121->134 over 112 cm) with a smeared image band.
evidence: 112 cm track entering through the top (2.6 cm from y=606), fit end at y=553 in APA1 (x=133.6, z=69): 53 cm below the top face, 131 cm from the cathode, 162 cm from the APA seam, 224 cm from the anode, so mid-volume. The profile is wavy (plateau ~4-5e4 with dips to 1e4 and 0 at s=19 and 36 cm), with a 4-point spike to 1.2e5 at s=11 cm right where a vertex carries the low-charge side piece 99009 (13-16 cm, ~5 cm off the body line); the last 10 cm sit at 2-6e4, within the track own wave range, so no Bragg rise at the end and no sustained collapse either. In f_meas the cluster charge ends at the stop end in U, V and W, with the U dead band at ~1180 well away from it; in the 3-D frames nothing continues past the end and the broad image cloud ends there too. Past the end, 99001 is a 3.6 cm stub at ~3e4 (below plateau) running nearly straight on (cos_fwd 0.93; the e azimuth shows a ~20 deg bend) - weak topology by itself, taken as the Michel because rule 3 holds. 99007 is a spur off the body at 27-31 cm and 99009 a low-charge spur at 13-16 cm, both on the muon side: delta / other. 318013 is a 2-point speck 55 cm back towards the entry, off in an unrelated direction: delta / other. Hard: the stub could be the muon own last cm (STM_ONLY), and the 11 cm spike could be read as an overshoot peak.

notes: ISOCHRONOUS: last ~110 cm at constant x, but rules 1 and 2 decide so the exception does not bite. Kind both rests on 331005 (chain label gamma body exclusion; I measure ~11 cm off the body line) - attached if it is read as body activity. Grey untabled trace at the stop noted.
evidence: 304 cm track entering 18.6 cm below the top face, fit end in APA3 at (21.7, 307, 365): 97 cm from the nearest face, 134 cm from the APA seam, 19 cm from the cathode. The end view shows the last ~110 cm running at constant x ~20 cm (near-isochronous lower section, horizontal in U and V of f_meas), so it runs parallel to the cathode rather than into it. The profile climbs cleanly: plateau ~4.5-5e4 at s=25-45 cm, ~7-8.5e4 over 5-20 cm, ~9.5-9.9e4 in the last 2 cm, following the muon curve shape - a clear Bragg rise to ~2x plateau. From the stop vertex a ~15 cm arm (107002 1.4-6.6 cm and 107003 6.6-15.4 cm, both shower-typed, cos_fwd -0.55/-0.77) leaves at an angle down and back beside the body; the d azimuth shows it clearly separated from the body line: the Michel. 107007 is a 2 cm piece at the vertex whose charge falls outwards (8.7e4 to 1.7e4), not several times the plateau, so no hot tip: michel. 331005 (2 pts, 22 cm) sits ~11 cm off the body in x, along the Michel arm direction: gamma. 330004 (4 pts, 37 cm) is forward and below the stop, ~90 deg from the Michel direction: delta / other. A grey dotted trace (~25 cm, not in the object table) also leaves the stop at an angle with a hook; unexplained but it cannot rescue a through-going muon given the rise.

notes: NO_MEASUREMENT: fit end and its tangle sit inside a V dead band in APA0 with patchy W, and the last 15 cm collapse to 0.2x plateau; DEAD: V dead band at the end; REVERSED: the fit end is the upper end of the track and the chain entry is at the bottom/cathode, so a downward cosmic cannot stop at the fit end unless it is upward-going (rare) - the fit end may instead be a vertex whose upstream is not imaged. Readings weighed: STM_MICHEL on the tangle (rule 1) vs THRU on the direction argument; neither has positive support. Supersedes my earlier THRU/low record for this key.
evidence: 147 cm track in APA0. The chain entry is at (-1.2, 15, 223): at the cathode and 7.8 cm above the bottom face. The fit end is at (-103, 102, 192): 94 cm from the nearest face, 100 cm from the cathode, 39 cm from the APA seam, so the fit end is the HIGH end of the track. The profile sits at ~6e4 at s=25-40 cm, then falls smoothly to ~1.3e4 (0.2x plateau) over s=12-20 cm and stays flat and low for the last 12 cm, with no Bragg peak anywhere near the end. In f_meas the end sits inside a V dead band (3495-3515), and the track runs along that band for the whole window; APA0 W charge appears only in a patch at the stop, and U charge is dim throughout. So the end region is not a usable measurement. Around the end, six chain-Michel pieces from other clusters (158/159/436, 3-15 cm, 0.7-1.5e4 except one 3.8e4) form a looping tangle within 13 cm. In the d azimuth they lie on the muon line past the end, spreading ~5 cm sideways in c and e: a curling electron, dead-band imaging filler, or the debris of an interaction vertex. 157011 and 158018 lie back along the body. Rule 3 fails (dead band swallows the end), the tangle cannot be trusted as topology inside a dead band, and there is no positive continuation evidence either.

notes: Kind detached dots rests on four faint specks; 291011 sits at x~0 beside the no-charge row 57007 and could belong to another object at the cathode. Broad smeared image band around the body (x changes 35 cm over 218 cm).
evidence: 218 cm track entering through the top (0.4 cm from y=606), fit end in APA2 at (-22.6, 555, 430): 32 cm from the z=462 face, 51 cm below the top, 20 cm from the cathode, 199 cm from the APA seam. The profile sits at ~5-5.5e4 at s=25-38 cm, climbs to ~6.5-8e4 over s=7-20 cm, and the last three points are 7.5e4, 1.04e5 and 1.28e5 (~2.3x plateau). A 4 cm dip at s=2-6 cm includes a zero and reads as a hole, not a collapse, so this is a ragged but real Bragg rise. In f_meas the V charge ends cleanly at the stop on live channels; W ends ~20 channels short of a dead band and U ends at a dead-band edge, but V settles it. The 3-D frames show nothing continuing past the end; the broad image band around the body also stops there. Nothing is attached at the stop and no piece lies within 10 cm. 288008 (2 cm, faint, 14 cm out, perpendicular, ~14 cm off the body line) is a detached dot: capture gamma. 290010 (25 cm, ~12 cm off the body), 289009 (31 cm, ~27 cm off in x) and 291011 (45 cm, ~30 cm off in x, at x~0) are isolated compact specks clear of the body within 60 cm: capture gammas in any direction. 57007 has no dQ/dx: degenerate, delta / other. 58001 (29 cm arm off the body at 35-41 cm) and 58006 (arm at 121 cm) are delta rays off the body.

notes: DEAD: the stop and the Michel arm sit in V and W dead bands, but the Bragg rise, the live-U hook and the absence of re-emerging charge on live W make the stop solid.
evidence: 69 cm track entering 5.3 cm below the top face, fit end in APA2 at (-42.9, 543, 309): 63 cm below the top, 40 cm from the cathode, 78 cm from the APA seam, 153 cm from the z face. The profile has a ~6.5e4 plateau at s=20-30 cm, then rises to a broad ~9e4 hump over s=3-12 cm (~1.4x), easing to 7e4 at the last point: a Bragg rise with ordinary terminal scatter, not a sustained collapse, so the pin stays. From the stop vertex a 13 cm arm (69003 0-6.8 cm plus 69010 6.8-8.8 cm) leaves at roughly 80-90 deg to the muon in all three azimuths. Its charge (~3-7e4, dipping to 2.8e4) is at or below the plateau, electron-like: the Michel. In f_meas the last few cm and the arm sit in V (5555-5600) and W (8945-8970) dead bands, but U is live there and shows the arm as a hook of real charge. Any straight continuation would re-emerge on live W channels below 8945 and live U, and the 3-D frames show none. 313011 (2 pts, 23 cm) and 317012 (2 pts, 51 cm) both lie forward, clear of the body and along the Michel arm direction (cos ~0.95 with it): gammas.

notes: FLAT_STOP: the call rests on rule 3 (mid-volume, charge ends in U/V/W, no dead band, nothing continues); the apparent 2x rise over the last 10 cm is contested by an equally high s=30-45 cm stretch (72008) likely inflated by side activity. Moderately low-angle track (x 283->290 over 60 cm) with a broad smeared image band; not isochronous enough to invoke the exception. Supersedes my earlier record for this key (notes prefix only).
evidence: 60 cm fairly horizontal track in APA0, entering through the z=0 face (8.6 cm) at y=410 and running +z to a fit end at (-290, 394, 58): 58 cm from the z face, ~62 cm inside the anode wire plane (face.x 68), 212 cm below the top, 287 cm from the cathode and 173 cm from the seam. The profile is very scattered, with two populations at every s. But the last 10 cm is uniformly high (~1.1-1.45e5 except the final 7e4 point), while s=10-30 cm sits mostly at ~3.5-6e4: roughly a 2x climb over the last 10 cm, above the muon curve. The complication is that s=30-45 cm (72008, where the vertex cluster and side arms near the entry sit) is just as high, so the plateau is ill-defined. In f_meas the charge ends at the stop end in U, V and W, and the nearest dead bands (U ~800, W 7098) lie 35+ channels past it. W charge is healthy here. The 3-D frames show nothing continuing past the end, and the broad image band around the body ends there too. No object lies within 40 cm of the stop. 72009 (arm), 72006 (shower-typed) and C322 (no charge, no PR segment) all sit 40-60 cm back at the entry end on the body line: delta / other. Hard: the rise is only clear relative to s=10-30 cm, but the rule-3 conditions (mid-volume, charge ends in all planes, no dead band, nothing continues) hold independently.

notes: DEAD: the fit end coincides with time slice ~5 in all three planes, the start of the readout frame (track continues towards the anode = earlier arrival), i.e. a readout-window coverage hole; flat profile, no rise. Competing reading: STM_ONLY FLAT_STOP if the frame edge is not where I think it is. The rubric does not name the readout-window edge as a trap.
evidence: 71 cm straight track: chain entry 16.3 cm below the top face, fit end in APA3 at (119.6, 549, 326): 57 cm below the top, 117 cm from the cathode, 95 cm from the APA seam, 238 cm from the anode face. The profile is flat at ~5.5-7e4 from s=45 cm right to the end, with the last two points slightly low (5.3e4, 4.6e4) and no climb at all. 118003 is a 3 cm stub straight on (cos_fwd 0.99) at ~2.5-3e4, below plateau. In f_meas the charge ends in U, V and W at the same place, well clear of the V dead band (5910) and the W dead line (9535). But that place is time slice ~5-8, the very start of the readout window, and the track runs towards the anode (smaller drift time) past the fit end, so its continuation would have arrived before the readout began. The stop end is where the window clips the track, not a measured end of charge. The 3-D frames show nothing past the end, as expected for clipped charge. No other object is near. The rule-3 conditions would otherwise make this a FLAT_STOP, so the call rests on reading the readout-window edge as a coverage hole swallowing the end.

notes: ISOCHRONOUS: x constant within 2.3 cm, rule 3 not applicable; the other end is at the bottom face (FACE exit), so the fit end is the upstream end of a downward track. Competing readings: UNCLEAR/NO_MEASUREMENT (wave profile, APA2 bottom corner), or STM_MICHEL taking 142004 as a backward Michel arm (chain view).
evidence: 32 cm near-vertical track at the bottom of APA2 (x=-273, z=253). The chain entry sits on the bottom face (0.1 cm from y=7.6), and the fit end is at y=43.7, 36 cm above the bottom face, 22 cm from the APA seam and 270 cm from the cathode. The track is near-isochronous: x changes 2.3 cm over its length, U and V see it as a flat line at t~1030, and W as a single blob. The profile is a smooth wave with nothing to read: 7.5e4 at the bottom-face end, falling to 1e4 at s=22, rising to ~3.5e4 at s=3-8 and 2.8e4 at the end. This is also the APA2 bottom corner where coverage holes are expected. Past the end, 28006 (7 cm, ~1.3e4) continues straight on (cos_fwd +1.0): weak, a muon continuation. 142004 (15 cm, other cluster, d 3.4-16 cm) runs parallel to the body ~4-5 cm off it, the whole length of the fit, and does not start at the stop vertex: it reads as an isochronous-imaging duplicate or a body delta, not a Michel. A downward cosmic touching the bottom face exits through it, so the fit end is the upper end of the visible track, and the stub continues past it. Hard: isochronous, coverage-hole region, no readable profile; the direction argument is the main evidence.

notes: FLAT_STOP: mid-volume by direction, charge ends in all planes, no dead band, nothing continues. Competing reading THRU (FACE:) because the end is 6.5 cm inside the z=0 face; rejected because the track runs parallel to that face at the end. MCS 44 MeV vs range 254 MeV fits a scattering, low-momentum end.
evidence: 101 cm wiggly track in APA0 entering through the top (0.4 cm from y=606) at x=-314, running down and towards the cathode while hugging the z=0 face (z 6-15 cm all along). Fit end at (-264, 543, 6.7): 6.5 cm inside the z=0 face, 63 cm below the top, 94 cm from the anode face, 262 cm from the cathode. Over its last ~20 cm the track moves in +x/-y at constant z ~6-7, i.e. parallel to that face, not out through it. The profile is flat and scattered at ~3-6e4 (APA0 scale) with dips to 1e4; the last two points are 5.8e4 and 6.5e4, with no climb over the last 10-20 cm. In f_meas the cluster charge ends at the stop end (t~1295) in U, V and W, with no dead band anywhere near. The 3-D frames show nothing continuing past the end, and no object starts at the stop and carries on. The chain delta rays 31014 (5-7.5 cm), 31011 (7.5-11 cm) and 31020 (11.5-14 cm) double the body a few cm off it, starting from body vertices, not the stop vertex: delta / other, as are the body arms 31027/31031/31017/31023 and the shower-typed 31028 at 25-52 cm. No Michel-like arm. Hard: flat profile, and the end is only 6.5 cm from a face, although it runs parallel to it.

notes: ANODE: fit end at |x|=351.8 cm (face.x 6.2), flat profile, no decay topology.
evidence: 396 cm track crossing the full drift length of the x<0 volume: chain entry at (-24, 581, 282), 24 cm from the cathode and 25 cm below the top; fit end at (-351.8, 442, 340) in APA2. face.x is 6.2 cm there, i.e. |x|=351.8 cm, at the anode wire plane, 164 cm from the bottom and 109 cm from the APA seam. The profile is flat and scattered at ~5-6e4 all the way in, with the last points at 7.3-8.1e4, then 1.3e4, 3e4 and 4e4 at the very end: no climb over the last 10-20 cm, just scatter. In f_meas the charge ends at the anode-side end (t~450) in all planes, which is where a track leaving through the anode ends. The 3-D frames show a small star of pieces at ~33 cm back on the body (37042 arm, 37043/37044 shower-typed, near 34 cm), plus delta rays 37038/37064 far up the body: all on the muon line, not at the stop, delta / other. 36065 is a degenerate 2-point row with no dQ/dx and its centroid at x=-373, outside the active volume: delta / other. 37050 (shower-typed) sits at the entry end. An end at the anode with a flat profile is an exit.

notes: ISOCHRONOUS: track hugs the anode plane at 3-8 cm drift, V collapses to one channel, rule 3 not applicable; charge continues straight on past the fit end in 39010. Competing reading UNCLEAR/NO_MEASUREMENT - the profile carries no Bragg information at all.
evidence: 38 cm track in APA2 lying along the anode plane. The chain entry is at |x|=349.1 (face.x 8.9, at the anode wire plane) and the fit end at (-344.1, 169, 318), |x|=344 (face.x 13.9), 162 cm above the bottom, 87 cm from the seam, 145 cm from the z face. The whole object sits 3-8 cm from the wires and is near-isochronous: x changes 5 cm over 38 cm, V sees it as a single vertical blob at one channel, U and W as short flat lines at t~1025-1045. The profile is low and wavy with nothing to read: ~2-3e4 over s=15-35 cm, dropping to ~1e4 and near zero over the last 12 cm, with no rise. 39010 (7.5 cm, fitted, cos_fwd 0.98) carries straight on past the fit end with real charge climbing outward from 1e4 to 2.7e4, back to the track own level, so the fit end is not where the charge ends. No arm leaves at an angle. 39007 (pion-typed, 5 cm) is the fitted continuation at the far entry end. The specks 182006 (41 cm), 38004 (no dQ/dx, centroid at x=-374 outside the volume) and 181005 (size 0, 57 cm) are degenerate or unrelated: delta / other.

notes: FACE: fit end 0.1 cm from the z=462 face and the entire track lies in that face plane (single W channel), fragmented; flat low profile; chain Michel 190003 is a straight-ahead fragment on the face.
evidence: 161 cm track lying in the plane of the back face in APA2: both ends and the whole body sit at z~462 (chain entry 0.3 cm and fit end 0.1 cm from the z=462 face). It runs from (-2.5, 318), at the cathode, down to the fit end at (-82.8, 187), 179 cm above the bottom and 80 cm from the cathode. W, the collection plane measuring z, sees the whole track on a single channel (~9280) at the edge of the wire plane. The 3-D image is broken into separate fragments with charge-free gaps, typical of a track drifting in and out of the active edge. The profile is low and gappy (~1-2.5e4, well under a normal MIP here) with no rise at the end. Past the fit end, 190003 (2 points, 15 cm, cos_fwd 0.96, the chain Michel) and the specks 184001 (20 cm) and 189002 (36 cm) sit along the same line on the face: fragments of the same edge-grazing track, not decay products. An end at a face with a flat profile is an exit, and here the whole track lies on the face.

notes: Pin left at the fit end. Competing reading OVERSHOOT with the stop at the arm vertex (~10 cm, where the 9.5e4 spike sits, followed by a 1-3e4 dip); rejected because an equally deep dip sits on the muon side at 12-18 cm, so the pattern reads as the APA0 wave rather than a peak-then-collapse. If the arm were read as body activity, rule 3 still gives a FLAT_STOP stopper.
evidence: 499 cm track entering through the top (1.2 cm), fit end mid-volume in APA0 at (-161, 174, 171): 166 cm above the bottom, 158 cm from the cathode, 60 cm from the APA seam, 170 cm from the z face, 197 cm from the anode face. The profile is an APA0-style wave with no Bragg rise: plateau ~5-7e4 at s=20-45 cm, a near-zero dip at s=12-18 cm, a 2-point spike to 9.5e4 at s~9, a second dip to 1-3e4 at s=3-7, then 5-6.5e4 at the end. In f_meas the charge ends at the stop end in U, V and W, with no dead band near; nothing continues past the end in the 3-D frames. At a body vertex ~10 cm before the fit end (d_min 9.2), a 22 cm arm 51014 (~2.9e4, below plateau) leaves at ~90 deg, clearly off the body line in all three azimuths. The chain carries straight on for the last ~12 cm (51047 low-charge, 51048). A muon within ~10 cm of its stop has too little energy to throw a 22 cm delta ray, so the arm reads as the decay electron: michel by the within-10 cm rule, since it is well clear of the body. All other delta/arm rows sit 45-290 cm back on the body: delta / other. Hard: the Michel joins ~10 cm before the fit end, so either the fit overshoots to that vertex or the last 12 cm is muon.

notes: CATHODE: the continuation past the fit end reaches x~0 (92017 at x=-0.2), so the object likely crosses into the other drift volume. REVERSED: the chain far (entry) end is mid-volume and is the real stop candidate; it cannot be judged here (V dead band, falling charge). Competing reading STM_MICHEL taking the 30-40 deg kink as decay topology (rule 1) with 93013 as a 22 cm Michel.
